summary:
*   **Purpose**: This section provides a step-by-step guide for determining the "Cost of Acquisition" of various capital assets when the previous market value cannot be used, which is essential for calculating Capital Gains Tax.
*   **General Rule for Inherited/Gifted Assets**: Under Clause 1, if an asset is acquired via gift, will, inheritance, company liquidation, or specific trust/company transfers, the cost is set at the **previous owner's original acquisition cost**, plus the value of any improvements made.
*   **Corporate Mergers**: Clause 2 specifies that for shares acquired during a company amalgamation (merger), the cost is the price paid for the shares in the **original (amalgamating) company**.
*   **Bond Debentures**: Clause 3 states that when debentures are converted into shares (as per section 70), the cost of the new shares is the **original cost of the debentures** that were converted.
*   **Special Securities & Equity**: Clause 4 establishes that for sweat equity or specific securities, the cost is based on the **Fair Market Value** used for tax purposes at the time of allotment.
*   **Partnerships & Redemptions**: Clauses 5 and 6 dictate that for LLC partners converting to a company, the cost is the value of the firm **before conversion**; for GDR redemptions, the cost is the **stock exchange price** on the day the redemption request was made.
*   **Trusts & Funds**: Clauses 7 and 8 assign the cost of units in business trusts or mutual fund consolidations to the **cost of the original assets** or shares that were swapped into the trust/fund.
*   **Preference Share Conversion**: Clause 9 mandates that when preference shares are converted into equity, the cost of the new equity is the **cost of the original preference shares** that were surrendered.

*   **Purpose**: This section defines the "Cost of Acquisition" for specific types of capital assets, which is a critical component for calculating capital gains tax liability.
*   **Mutual Fund Units (Section 10)**: For units acquired through the consolidation of a mutual fund scheme under Section 70(1)(zk), the cost of acquisition is the original cost of the units in the originating scheme.
*   **Segregated Portfolio Units (Section 11 & 12)**: The cost for units in a segregated portfolio is calculated using a specific formula (Original Cost × NAV of transferred assets / Total NAV before segregation). Conversely, the cost of the remaining original units in the main portfolio is reduced by the amount so calculated.
*   **Joint Venture Shares (Section 13)**: The cost of acquisition for shares as referred to in Section 70(1)(zl) is based on the cost of the original interest in the joint venture.
*   **Demerger Shares (Section 14 & 15)**: For a demerger, the cost of shares in the new (resulting) company is determined by a formula based on the net book value of transferred assets and the net worth of the original company. The cost of the shareholder's original shares in the demerged company is reduced by this allocated amount.
*   **Specific Scenarios (Sections 16–18)**:
    *   Assets deemed chargeable under Section 71(1) use the cost acquired by the transferee company.
    *   Properties where value was assessed under Section 92(2)(m) use that assessed value.
    *   Assets declared under the Income Declaration Scheme, 2016 (with tax/penalty paid) use the fair market value taken into account during the scheme.
*   **Specified Capital Assets (Section 19)**: For covered real estate transferred after two years have passed since possession was handed over (per Section 10(37A) of the Income-tax Act), the cost of acquisition is the stamp duty value as of the last day of that second tax year.

summary:
*   **Purpose and Scope**: This section defines the "full value of consideration" or specific valuation metrics for various capital assets under the Income-tax Act, including shares in joint development projects, trust assets, Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs), and gold released against EGRs.
*   **Gilt-Edge and Project Valuations (Sub-sections 20–21)**: For shares in projects involving land or buildings (Sec 67(14)), the value is the deemed full consideration. For trust assets, the value is the fair market value of the asset considered for computing accreted income as per Sec 352(3).
*   **Gold-Related Assets (Sub-sections 22–24)**:
    *   **EGRs**: If an Electronic Gold Receipt issued by a Vault Manager becomes property via transfer (Sec 70(1)(y)), the relevant value is the cost of the gold in the recipient's name.
    *   **Released Gold**: If physical gold is released against an EGR as consideration for a transfer (Sec 70(1)(y)), the relevant value is the cost of the EGR held by the recipient.
*   **Definition Clarifications (Sub-section 2)**:
    *   **"Previous Owner"**: Defined specifically for assets held by trusts/charitable institutions (Serial No. 1) to identify the last owner who acquired it via a non-exempt mode.
    *   **SEBI Portfolios**: Terms like "main" and "segregated" portfolio carry the meanings assigned in SEBI Circular dated 28 Dec 2018.
    *   **Net Worth**: For demerger cases (Serial Nos. 14–15), defined as the sum of paid-up share capital and general reserves in the demerged company's books immediately before the transaction.
*   **Application to Co-operative Banks (Sub-section 2(d))**: The specific valuation provisions and definitions listed for Serial Nos. 2, 14, and 15 also apply to business reorganizations of co-operative banks under Section 65.
*   **Depreciable Block of Assets (Section 74)**: Overrides general deprecation rules for assets on which depreciation was allowed under the Income-tax Act, 1961 or 1922.
*   **Short-Term Capital Gains on Block Transfers (Section 74(2))**: If the sale consideration for any asset in a block exceeds the sum of (a) transfer expenses, (b) the block’s written-down value at the start of the year, and (c) the cost of any new assets acquired in the block during the year, the excess is deemed **short-term** capital gains.
*   **Complete Sale of a Block (Section 74(3))**: If *all* assets in a block are sold, the cost of acquisition is the initial written-down value plus the cost of any assets acquired during the year, and the entire income from the transfer is deemed **short-term** capital gains.

section_header: 75. If depreciation has been obtained under section 33(2) for a capital asset in | Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004.
summary:
*   **Depreciable Asset Valuation (Section 75):** If you have already claimed depreciation on a capital asset, this section modifies the calculation of capital gains (under Sections 72 and 73) by treating the asset's "written down value" (as defined in Section 41) as its cost of acquisition, rather than the original purchase price.
*   **Short-Term Capital Gains for Specific Assets (Section 76):** Gains from the transfer, redemption, or maturity of specific financial instruments are strictly classified as **short-term capital gains**, regardless of the holding period. This applies to:
    *   Units of "Specified Mutual Funds" (debt-focused funds) acquired on or after April 1, 2023, or Market Linked Debentures.
    *   Unlisted bonds or debentures transferred, redeemed, or maturing on or after July 23, 2024.
*   **Calculation Formula for Section 76 Assets:** The taxable short-term gain ($X$) is calculated as: **$X = A - B - C$**, where $A$ is the total consideration received, $B$ is the cost of acquisition, and $C$ is expenditure incurred wholly and exclusively for the transaction.
*   **STT Deduction Prohibition:** No deduction is allowed for Securities Transaction Tax (STT) paid on transactions covered under Section 76.
*   **Definitions for Section 76:**
    *   **Market Linked Debenture:** A debt security with returns linked to market returns or indices, as regulated by SEBI.
    *   **Specified Mutual Fund:** A fund investing >65% in debt/money market instruments (or in other such funds), measured by the annual average of daily closing figures.
*   **Slump Sale Classification (Section 77):** Profits from a "slump sale" (sale of a business undertaking or division as a whole) are treated as capital gains. They are deemed **long-term** unless the asset was held for 36 months or less, in which case they are **short-term**.
*   **Valuation and Reporting for Slump Sales (Section 77):**
    *   **Cost Basis:** The "net worth" of the undertaking replaces the cost of acquisition. "Net worth" is total assets (using written down value for depreciable assets and nil for self-generated goodwill) minus liabilities, ignoring revaluation changes.
    *   **Consideration:** The fair market value of the assets on the transfer date is deemed the consideration received.
    *   **Compliance:** You must furnish a report by a qualified accountant certifying the net worth calculation before the specified filing date.

section_header: 80. If the consideration received or accruing from the transfer of a capital asset | 81. Where any capital asset was, on any previous occasion, the subject of (Part 1)
summary:
*   **Valuation by Fair Market Value (Section 80):** When the consideration for transferring a capital asset is not ascertainable or determinable, the fair market value on the date of transfer is deemed as the full value of consideration for computing capital gains.
*   **Deduction of Advance Payments (Section 81):** Any advance or money received and retained during prior negotiations for the transfer of a capital asset must be deducted from the cost of acquisition (or written down value/fair market value) when computing capital gains. However, this deduction does not apply if the amount has already been included in the total income under Section 92(2)(h).
*   **Exemption for Residential House Investment (Section 82(1)):** Individuals or Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) can exempt long-term capital gains from tax if they purchase one residential house in India within one year before or two years after the transfer, or construct one within three years after the transfer.
*   **Treatment of Excess or Unused Gains (Section 82(1) & 82(4)):** If the capital gain exceeds the cost of the new house, the excess is taxed. If the gain is less than or equal to the new house's cost, the new house's cost is reduced by the gain amount. Any unutilized deposited amount after three years becomes taxable income in the year the period expires.
*   **Required Deposit of Unused Gains (Section 82(2)):** To claim the exemption, any capital gain not immediately used for the new asset must be deposited in a specified bank/institution before the due date of filing the income tax return, with proof of deposit submitted with the return.
*   **Option for Multiple Assets and High-Value Limits (Section 82(5)–82(8)):** If the gain is ₹2 crore or less, taxpayers may purchase two residential houses instead of one (exercisable once per taxpayer). Additionally, the exemption is capped: costs exceeding ₹10 crore for the new asset and gains exceeding ₹10 crore are not considered for the exemption.
*   **Exemption for Agricultural Land (Section 83(1)):** Capital gains from the transfer of agricultural land used by the assessee (or their parent/HUF) for two years prior to transfer are not charged if the proceeds are used to purchase other agricultural land within two years after the transfer.

section_header: 81. Where any capital asset was, on any previous occasion, the subject of (Part 2)
summary:
*   **Section 81(b)–(d) Purpose & Penalties (Residential Assets):** This section addresses the tax exemption for capital gains when an asset is sold to buy a new residential property. It includes strict "clawback" provisions: if the taxpayer purchases or constructs another income-generating residential house within specific time limits (2 years for purchase, 3 years for construction), or if they sell the new asset within 3 years, the previously exempted gain becomes chargeable as long-term capital gains in that year.
*   **Section 81(g)–(h) Monetary Cap:** The benefit of these capital gains exemptions is capped; any portion of the new asset's cost *or* the original sale consideration (net consideration) that exceeds ₹10 Crores is ineligible for the exemption set out in sub-sections (1) and (2).
*   **Section 81(h) Definition of "Net Consideration":** Defined as the full value received from the sale of the original asset, minus any expenditure incurred wholly and exclusively for that transfer.
*   **Section 87(a) Purpose (Industrial Relocation):** Provides a mechanism to defer capital gains tax when an industrial undertaking is shifted from an urban area to a non-urban area and associated capital assets (machinery, plant, land, or building) are sold.
*   **Section 87(b) Re-investment Window & Options:** The taxpayer must use the proceeds within 1 year before or 3 years after the transfer to purchase new machinery/plant, acquire/construct buildings/land, or physically shift the original asset to the new area to qualify for deferral.
*   **Section 87(1) Tax Computation Logic:** If the cost of the new reinvestment is less than the capital gain, the difference is taxed immediately. If it equals or exceeds the gain, no gain is charged immediately. However, if the *new* asset is sold within 3 years, its base cost for tax purposes is reduced by the amount of the deferred gain.
*   **Section 87(2)–(4) Deposit & Failure Mechanism:** If the full amount is not utilized immediately, the unused portion must be deposited in a specified bank/institution by the income tax return filing deadline. Any amount not utilized for the new asset within the prescribed period is treated as taxable income in the year the 3-year window expires (sub-section 4).

section_header: 89. Irrespective of anything contained in sections 82, 83, 84, 85, and 86,–– (Part 1)
summary:
*   **Timing Extension for Compulsory Acquisitions (Section 89)**: If a capital asset is acquired compulsorily under any law and compensation is not received by the transfer date, the deadline for reinvesting capital gains (under Sections 82–86) starts from the date of actual receipt of compensation, not the original transfer date.
*   **Nil Cost for Intangibles (Section 90(1)(a))**: The "cost of improvement" is defined as **nil** for intangible assets, including goodwill, manufacturing rights, business rights, and other similar intangible property.
*   **Calculation of Improvement Costs (Section 90(1)(b))**: For tangible assets, "cost of improvement" generally includes capital expenditure on additions or alterations. For assets owned prior to April 1, 2001, only expenses incurred on or after that date count; for other assets, all post-acquisition capital expenses apply.
*   **Exclusion of Income-Deductible Expenses (Section 90(2))**: The "cost of improvement" explicitly **excludes** any expenditure that is already deductible as a business expense, house property expense, or other income source deduction, preventing double dipping.
*   **Special Rules for Intangible Asset Acquisition Costs (Section 90(3))**: The "cost of acquisition" for intangibles (e.g., trademarks, business rights, permits) is typically the purchase price. However, it is deemed **nil** if the asset was not acquired by purchase from the previous owner.
*   **Depreciation Adjustment for Pre-2020 Intangibles (Section 90(4))**: If an asset like goodwill was acquired by purchase and depreciation was claimed under the Income-tax Act in a tax year prior to April 1, 2020, the total pre-2020 depreciation must be **subtracted** from the purchase price to determine the cost of acquisition.
*   **Treatment of Bonus Shares/Allotments (Section 90(5)-(6))**: When an assessee acquires additional financial assets (shares/securities) via subscription rights or free allotment:
    *   The cost of the original asset remains the actual purchase price.
    *   The cost of assets allotted **without payment** is deemed **nil**.
    *   If the subscription right is renounced to another person, the cost for that person is the purchase price paid to the renouncer plus any payment made to the company.
*   **Grandfathering Clause for Pre-2018 Equity Shares (Section 90(7))**: For equity shares, equity-oriented fund units, or business trust units acquired before February 1, 2018, the cost of acquisition is the **higher** of the actual purchase price or the lower of the Fair Market Value (FMV) and the transfer consideration.

section_header: 89. Irrespective of anything contained in sections 82, 83, 84, 85, and 86,–– (Part 2)
summary:
**Section 89 (Part 2) & Sections 93–94: Exemptions, Definitions, and Deductions**

*   **Exceptions to Transfer Valuation (Section 89(2)–(3)):** Specific property transfers are excluded from standard capital gains valuation rules, including transfers by non-profit organizations (Section 355(g)), transactions not considered "transfers" under Section 70(1), and transfers from an individual to a trust established solely for their relatives.
*   **Immovable Property Valuation Rules (Section 89(4)):** If the stamp duty value is disputed, the Assessing Officer may refer the matter to a Valuation Officer. Where the agreement date and registration date differ, the stamp duty value on the *agreement date* applies only if full or partial payment was made via account payee instruments or electronic banking modes on or before the agreement date.
*   **Key Definitions (Section 89(5)):** The section defines critical terms such as "property" (encompassing land, building, shares, securities, jewellery, art, bullion, and virtual digital assets), "relative" (detailed kinship rules for individuals and HUFs), and "lottery" (including prize-based games and shows).
*   **Deductions from "Income from Other Sources" (Section 93(1)):** Assessable income can be reduced by reasonable expenses for realizing dividends/interest, 50% of certain capital gains (Section 92(2)(i)), and one-third of family pension income (capped at ₹25,000 if tax is deducted at source, or ₹15,000 otherwise).
*   **General Expense Deduction (Section 93(1)(e)):** Taxpayers may deduct any expenditure laid out wholly and exclusively for earning this income, provided it is not a capital expenditure.
*   **Restricted Deductions for Dividends and Mutual Funds (Section 93(2)):** No deductions are allowed for dividends falling under Section 2(40)(f). For other dividends, Mutual Fund units, or Specified Company units, the *only* allowable deduction is interest expense, limited to 20% of the gross income for that tax year.
*   **Prohibition of Deductions (Section 94(1)):** Certain amounts listed in Section 94 are explicitly prohibited from being deducted when computing income chargeable under this head, overriding the general permissions in Section 93.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B; or | Chapter XIX-B. | 95. The provision of section 38(1)(a) shall apply in computing the income of | 96. All income arising to any person by virtue of transfer,–– | 98. For the purposes of sections 96 and 97, and this section,—
summary:
**Summary of Sections 94–99 (Anti-Avoidance and Income Attribution Rules)**

*   **Treatment of Other Income Sources (S. 94):** Income from "other sources" is computed using the same rules as business income (e.g., allowing deductions under Sections 29, 35, and 36); however, **no deductions** are allowed for gambling, lottery, or betting winnings, with a specific exception for the maintenance costs of racehorses (S. 94(4)-(5)).
*   **Specific Provisions for Foreign Companies & Transfer Pricing (S. 94-95):** Section 59 (special provisions for business profits) applies to "other sources" income for foreign companies (S. 94(3)), and Section 38(1)(a) applies to computing income for assesses subject to transfer pricing rules under Section 92 (S. 95).
*   **Income from Transfer of Rights Without Assets (S. 96):** If a person transfers the right to receive income without transferring the underlying assets generating that income, the resulting income is fully taxable in the hands of the **transferor**, regardless of whether the transfer is revocable or occurred before/after the Act's commencement.
*   **Revocable Transfers of Assets (S. 97):** Income arising from assets transferred via a **revocable** arrangement is taxed as the income of the **transferor**. This rule does not apply if the transfer is irrevocable during the lifetime of the beneficiary (in trust) or the transferee, and the transferor derives no direct or indirect benefit from the income.
*   **Reversal of Revoked Transfers (S. 97(3)):** If the power to revoke a transfer arises later, any income arising as a result of that power becoming effective is immediately chargeable as the income of the **transferor**.
*   **Definition of "Transfer" and "Revocable" (S. 98):** "Transfer" broadly includes settlements, trusts, covenants, agreements, or arrangements. A transfer is deemed **revocable** if it allows for the direct or indirect re-transfer of income/assets to the original owner or if it retains any power over such assets.
*   **Attribution of Family Member Income (S. 99):** The total income of an individual includes:
    1.  Income of the **spouse** from salary in a concern where the individual has a substantial interest (excluding income solely from the spouse's professional skills) or from assets transferred without adequate consideration.
    2.  Income of the **son's wife** from assets transferred on or after June 1, 1973, without adequate consideration.
    3.  Income of a **minor child**, *unless* the income arises from the child's manual work, specialized skill/talent, or the child has a disability as specified.

summary:
*   **Liability for Included Income (Section 100):** If the income of a third party (from an asset or firm membership) is included in the assessee's total income, that third party becomes personally liable to pay the corresponding tax upon notice; joint asset holders are jointly and severally liable, with recovery provisions from Chapter XIX-D applying.
*   **Inclusion of Tax-Exempt Income (Section 101):** Any income that is not subject to income tax under Chapter XVIIA-4 must still be included in the assessee’s total income for computation purposes.
*   **Unexplained Credits & Evidentiary Burden (Section 102):** Sums found in books of accounts without a satisfactory explanation are treated as taxable income. For loans/borrowings or share capital in private companies, the explanation is deemed unsatisfactory unless the lender/shareholder also provides a satisfactory explanation, thereby shifting part of the evidentiary burden to the source of funds.
*   **Venture Capital Exception (Section 102(4)):** The joint explanation requirements in Section 102(2) and (3) do not apply if the person providing the credit is a recognized Venture Capital Fund or Venture Capital Company.
*   **Unexplained Investments (Section 103):** Assets or investments not recorded in books, or recorded at amounts lower than actual value, are deemed taxable income if the assessee cannot provide a satisfactory explanation of their nature and source.
*   **Unexplained Assets (Section 104):** Any physical asset (including money, bullion, jewelry, or virtual digital assets) found in the possession of the assessee without book entries or satisfactory explanation is deemed to be income for the year it was discovered.
*   **Unexplained Expenditure Deduction Bar (Section 105):** Expenditure without a verified source is deemed taxable income, and this amount is strictly disallowed as a deduction under the Act, preventing the assessee from claiming relief for the same sum.
*   **Cash Borrowings/Repayments (Section 106):** Borrowing or repaying amounts via negotiable instruments (other than account payee cheques) or otherwise specified modes results in the amount being deemed income for the person borrowing or repaying.

CHAPTER VII (Part 1)
summary:
*   **Tax Assessment Basis (Section 107):** Income specified in sections 102 through 106 is subject to tax according to the provisions of Section 195.
*   **Intra-Head Loss Set-Off (Section 108):**
    *   Non-capital gains losses can be offset against **any other income source under the same head** in the same tax year (e.g., a loss from one salary source offsets another salary income).
    *   **Long-term capital losses** may only be set off against gains from other long-term capital assets.
    *   **Short-term capital losses** may be set off against gains from any capital asset (long-term or short-term).
*   **Inter-Head Loss Set-Off Restrictions (Section 109):**
    *   Generally, non-capital gains losses can be set off against income under **any other head**, including capital gains.
    *   **Exceptions:** Business losses **cannot** be set off against salary income; and house property losses are limited to an offset of ₹2 lakh against other heads.
    *   **Strict Prohibition:** Capital gains losses **cannot** be set off against income from any other head.
*   **Carry-Forward of House Property Losses (Section 110):** Unabsorbed house property losses can be carried forward for **up to 8 years** and must be set off only against future house property income.
*   **Carry-Forward of Capital Losses (Section 111):** Unabsorbed capital losses can be carried forward for **up to 8 years**. Long-term losses apply only to future long-term gains, while short-term losses apply to gains from any capital asset.
*   **Carry-Forward of Business Losses (Section 112):** Unabsorbed business losses (excluding speculation) can be carried forward for **up to 8 years** and must be set off only against future business or profession profits. These losses take priority over other carried-forward allowances (under sections 33(11) or 45(7)).
*   **Speculation Business Losses (Section 113):** Losses from speculation business are strictly confined to the same head; they can only be set off against profits from **another speculation business** in the current year or carried forward for future years under similar restrictions.

section_header:
195. 
CHAPTER VII (Part 2)
summary:
*   **Purpose**: This section (specifically **Section 117**) establishes special tax provisions to allow the transfer of accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation to successor entities resulting from the amalgamation of specific institutional types, including banking companies, State Bank of India-derived new banks, and Government insurance companies.
*   **Eligibility & Transfer of Benefits**: Under **Section 117(1)**, when eligible entities (such as banking companies merged via Central Government schemes or strategic disinvestments within five years) amalgamate, their accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation are deemed to be the losses/allowances of the **successor entity** (the new or absorbing bank/company) for the tax year the amalgamation takes effect.
*   **Carry-Forward Limitation**: For amalgamation schemes effective on or after **April 1, 2025**, **Section 117(2)** restricts the carry-forward of these deemed losses. The losses can only be carried forward in the hands of the successor entity for a maximum period of **eight tax years** immediately following the tax year in which the original predecessor entity first computed the loss.
*   **Application of General Rules**: Once the losses and depreciation are transferred to the successor entity as described, all other provisions of the Income Tax Act regarding the **set-off and carry-forward** of these amounts apply accordingly.
*   **Key Definitions**: **Section 117(3)** and the preceding text define critical terms:
    *   **“Accumulated Loss”**: Losses under the head “Profits and gains of business or profession” (excluding speculation business losses) that would have been eligible for set-off had the non-occurrence of the reorganization.
    *   **“Specified Bank”**: Includes the State Bank of India, banks constituted under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 or 1980.
    *   **“Original Predecessor Entity”**: The entity involved in the first amalgamation or reorganization in a series.
*   **Exceptions/Scope**: This section applies **irrespective** of general provisions in Section 2(6)(a) to (c) and Section 116, overriding standard rules to facilitate these specific public-sector or banking-sector mergers.

DEDUCTIONS TO BE MADE IN COMPUTING TOTAL INCOME
summary:
*   **General Deduction Framework (Sec 121(1) & (2)):** This section establishes that specific deductions are subtracted from "Gross Total Income" (defined in Sec 121(10) as income before these deductions) to compute Total Income. A strict cap is imposed: the aggregate amount of all deductions allowed under this Chapter cannot exceed the assessee’s Gross Total Income.
*   **Prevention of Double Benefits for Groups (Sec 121(3)):** If a deduction under specific sections (133, 135, 137, 138, 141, 142, or 143) is allowed to an Association of Persons (AOP) or Body of Individuals (BOI), the individual members cannot claim the same deduction against their respective share of income.
*   **Exclusivity and Cap for Business Deductions (Sec 121(4)):** For profits/gains from specific undertakings or eligible businesses, any deduction claimed under the "Deductions in respect of certain incomes" heading must be exclusive (no other deductions allowed under the Act for that same income) and cannot exceed the actual profits/gains of that specific business.
*   **Compliance Condition for Part C Deductions (Sec 121(5)):** Taxpayers are denied deductions under Part C of this Chapter if they fail to file their income tax return on or before the due date (under Sec 263(1)) or if they fail to explicitly claim the deduction in that return.
*   **Arm's Length Pricing for Inter-Business Transfers (Sec 121(6) & (7)):** When goods or services are transferred between a business eligible for Part C deductions and any other business of the same assessee, the profits are calculated as if the transfer occurred at "market value." This prevents under-valuation in internal accounts to artificially inflate profits for deduction purposes.
*   **Interaction with Section 46 (Sec 121(8)):** If a deduction is claimed under Part C for a "specified business" (as defined in Sec 46(11)(d)), no deduction is permitted under Section 46 for that business for the same year or any other year, preventing overlapping tax benefits.
*   **Standardized Income Calculation for Deductions (Sec 121(9)):** When computing the amount of income eligible for Part C deductions, the figure to be used is the income computed before any deductions under this Chapter are applied, ensuring consistency and preventing cascading deduction errors.

section_header: 123. An individual or a Hindu undivided family, shall be allowed a (Part 1)
summary:
*   **Eligibility & Threshold for Section 123**: Individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) can claim a tax deduction for specific investments (such as life insurance, provident funds, and deferred annuities) listed in Schedule XV, capped at **₹1,50,000** per tax year.
*   **Employer Pension Contributions (Sec. 124(1))**: Employees are entitled to a deduction for amounts contributed by their employer into a Central Government-notified pension scheme, limited to **14%** of salary for Central/State Government employers and **10%** for other private employers.
*   **Individual Pension Deposits (Sec. 124(3))**: Individuals may claim an additional deduction of up to **₹50,000** for amounts personally deposited into such notified pension schemes.
*   **Guardianship of Minors (Sec. 124(4))**: Guardians can claim deductions for deposits made to a minor’s pension account, but the combined total claimed by the guardian for the minor and themselves under Section 124(3) cannot exceed **₹50,000**.
*   **Taxation Upon Exit (Sec. 124(6))**: Amounts withdrawn from the pension scheme (including accrued interest) upon closure or opting out are **deemed income** and taxed in the year of receipt; however, death benefits received by nominees under specific circumstances (Sec. 124(7)-(8)) are exempt from this taxation.
*   **Tie-Back to Annuity Purchase (Sec. 124(9))**: Withdrawn amounts are not deemed taxable income in the same tax year if they are immediately used to purchase an annuity plan.
*   **No Double Deduction (Sec. 124(10))**: Taxpayers cannot claim a deduction under Section 123 for amounts that have already been claimed as a deduction under Section 124(3).
*   **Agniveer Specific Deduction (Sec. 125)**: Individuals enrolled in the Agnipath Scheme are eligible for a full deduction on contributions made to the **Agniveer Corpus Fund** and any matching contributions made by the Central Government to the same fund.

section_header: 123. An individual or a Hindu undivided family, shall be allowed a (Part 2)
summary:
*   **Medical Expense Deduction Adjustments (Sec. 123(3)-(5)):** The tax deduction for medical expenses is reduced by any amount reimbursed by insurance or an employer. Additionally, for senior citizen members of an individual or Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), the deduction amount is increased from ₹40,000 to ₹1,00,000.
*   **Higher Education Loan Interest (Sec. 129):** An individual can claim a deduction for interest paid on loans taken from approved financial or charitable institutions for their own or a relative's higher education. This deduction is available for the initial tax year and the seven subsequent tax years, or until the interest is fully paid, whichever is earlier.
*   **First-Home Buyer Deduction (Sec. 130):** Individuals are eligible for a deduction of up to ₹50,000 on interest paid for residential house property acquisition. This benefits loans sanctioned between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2017, provided the loan amount does not exceed ₹35 Lakh, the property value does not exceed ₹50 Lakh, and the borrower does not own any other residential property.
*   **Prohibition on Duplicate Claims (Sec. 130(4)):** If a deduction is claimed under Section 130, no other deduction can be claimed for the same loan interest under any other provision of the tax law for that or any other tax year.
*   **Secondary Housing Deduction (Sec. 131(1)-(2)):** Individuals not eligible for the Section 130 deduction may claim a higher deduction of up to ₹1,50,000 on loan interest for residential property. This applies to loans sanctioned between April 1, 2019, and March 31, 2022, subject to specific conditions regarding stamp duty value and other criteria (note: provided text is cut off in the source).
*   **Key Definitions:** "Financial institution" generally refers to banking companies under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, or specific housing finance companies (Sec. 130(5)). "Dependant" follows the definition in Section 127, and "higher education" refers to courses pursued after Senior Secondary examination from recognized institutions (Sec. 129(3)).

*   **Purpose:** These sections (134(5), 135, 136, and 137) establish tax deductions for specific charitable and political contributions, defining eligibility criteria, payment methods, and verification procedures.
*   **Research Deduction Cap (Section 134(5)):** For calculating deductions under the related section (implied Section 80-G context or similar pre-135 provision), limits of "10% of total income" or "25% of total income" are calculated based on total income *before* claiming this specific deduction.

*   **Individual/HUF Political Contribution Deduction (Section 137):** Any assessee (excluding local authorities and government-funded juridical persons) is allowed a deduction for non-cash contributions to registered political parties or electoral trusts.

section_header: 138. In respect of any tax year beginning on or after the 1st April, 2026, | 139. In respect of any tax year, where––
summary:
*   **Continuation of Phase-out Deductions**: Sections 138 and 139 ensure that tax incentives originally provided under the repealed Income-tax Act, 1961 continue to apply. Section 138 preserves deductions under Section 80-IA for infrastructure development businesses for tax years beginning on or after April 1, 2026, while Section 139 preserves deductions under Section 80-IAB for developers of Special Economic Zones.
*   **Start-up Tax Incentive**: Section 140 grants eligible start-ups a deduction of 100% of their business profits. This benefit is available for any three consecutive tax years selected within the first ten years from the date of incorporation (Section 140(1) & (2)).
*   **Eligibility Restrictions**: To qualify as an "eligible start-up," the business must not be formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business, nor by transferring previously used machinery or plant to the new entity (Section 140(3)).
*   **Exception for Business Interruption**: The prohibition on splitting up existing businesses (Section 140(3)(a)) does not apply if a business was discontinued due to natural disasters (e.g., floods, earthquakes), riots, accidental fires, or enemy action, and is subsequently re-established or revived within three years (Section 140(4)).
*   **Imported Machinery Exemption**: Machinery or plant imported from outside India is considered "new" for the purposes of Section 140(3)(b) only if it was never used in India prior to installation and no depreciation was previously claimed on it by any person (Section 140(5)).

section_header: 141. In respect of any tax year, where–– | 142. In respect of any tax year, where––
summary:
*   **Continuity of Industrial Deductions (Section 141):** Assessees with income from businesses that were eligible for deductions under Section 80-IB of the repealed Income-tax Act, 1961, are allowed equivalent deductions in the new tax year. The amount and duration of these deductions must strictly follow the calculations and timelines that would have applied under the old law.
*   **Continuity of Housing Project Deductions (Section 142):** Similarly, for businesses involved in developing or building housing projects and rental housing projects, deductions previously available under Section 80-IBA of the repealed Act are preserved. These deductions are calculated and permitted only for the tax years originally eligible under the old provisions.
*   **100% Tax Holiday for North-Eastern States (Section 143(1)):** Undertakings carrying out specific eligible businesses in the North-Eastern States are entitled to a deduction of 100% of their profits and gains. This tax holiday is valid for ten consecutive tax years starting from the initial tax year of operation.
*   **Eligibility Period and Scope (Section 143(2)):** To claim the benefits under Section 143, an undertaking must begin its operations (manufacturing, substantial expansion, or eligible business activities) between April 1, 2007, and April 1, 2017, within any of the North-Eastern States.
*   **Anti-Avoidance Conditions (Section 143(3)):** The benefits are denied if the undertaking is merely a split-up, reconstruction, or transfer of an existing business using previously used machinery or plant. However, this restriction does not apply if the business is a genuine revival of another undertaking as specifically permitted under Section 140(4).
*   **Exclusive Benefit Provision (Section 143(5)):** While the provided text is cut off, the section indicates an exclusivity clause where, irrespective of other provisions, no other deductions under the Act may be allowed in computing the total income for the period covered by this specific 100% deduction, likely preventing double-birding of tax incentives.

summary:
*   **Purpose of Section 144:** This section provides tax incentives to entrepreneurs in Special Economic Zones (SEZs) who manufacture goods or provide services, effectively extending the benefits previously available under the repealed Income-tax Act if they were focused on exports.
*   **Deduction Conditions (Section 144):** The allowable deduction must be calculated exactly as it would have been under Section 10AA of the old Income-tax Act, 1961, and is limited to specific tax years that would have qualified under the previous legislation.
*   **General Deduction Limits (Clause 6):** No deduction is allowed if the total period of deductions (combined with any prior deductions under Section 80-IB(4) of the old Act) exceeds ten tax years.
*   **Restricted Goods (Clause 8(a)):** Tax benefits are not available for "eligible articles" that include tobacco products, pan masala, plastic carry bags thinner than 20 microns, or goods produced by petroleum and gas refineries.
*   **Eligible Businesses (Clause 8(b)):** Specific business types qualify for these incentives, including hotels (2-star or above), adventure/leisure sports, nursing homes (25+ beds), old-age homes, specific vocational training institutes (e.g., aviation, nursing, IT), IT hardware manufacturing, and bio-technology.
*   **Key Definitions (Clause 8):** "Substantial expansion" is defined as a 25% increase in plant and machinery investment, and "North-Eastern States" is explicitly listed to define the geographic scope for certain regulatory contexts within the Act.
*   **Additional Incentives (Sections 145-146):** Separate provisions grant a 100% deduction for five years for businesses processing bio-degradable waste (Section 145) and a 30% deduction for three years on additional employee costs (Section 146), provided the business is not a result of splitting or acquiring an existing entity.

summary:
*   **Purpose of Section 147 (Deductions for Offshore Banking Units/IFSC Units):** This section provides tax deductions for income generated by Offshore Banking Units (OBUs) and units of the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), including specific allowances for assets like aircraft or ships leased by units that commenced operations by March 31, 2030.
*   **Compliance Requirements (Section 147(4)):** To claim deductions under Section 147, the assessee must submit a return of income that includes an accountant’s report certifying the claim and a copy of the relevant permission or registration (from the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, or the IFSC Authority Act, 2019).
*   **Key Definition - "Relevant Tax Year" (Section 147(5)(a)):** The "relevant tax year" for OBU/IFSC entities is defined as the year in which the necessary permissions or registrations under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, SEBI Act, 1992, or IFSC Authority Act, 2019, were obtained.
*   **Purpose of Section 148 (Inter-Corporate Dividend Deduction):** This section allows domestic companies to deduct dividends received from other domestic companies, foreign companies, or business trusts. The deduction is limited to the amount of dividends distributed by the receiving company by one month before the due date for filing its return of income.
*   **Anti-Double Counting Rule (Section 148(2)):** Once a deduction is allowed in a tax year for dividends distributed by a domestic company under Section 148(1), no further deduction can be claimed for that same amount in any other tax year.
*   **Purpose of Section 149 (Co-operative Society Deductions):** This section allows co-operative societies to deduct certain sums from their gross total income when computing total income, specifically targeting profits from member-focused activities to support the cooperative sector.
*   **Full Deductions for Specific Cooperative Activities (Section 149(2)(a) & (b)):** Co-operative societies are entitled to a *full* deduction on profits and gains from specified activities, including banking/credit, cottage industries, agricultural marketing, and supplying milk, oilseeds, fruits, or vegetables to federal societies, the Government, or government companies.
*   **Tiered Deductions for Other Activities (Section 149(2)(c)):** For co-operative societies engaged in activities not listed in clauses (a) or (b), a limited deduction is allowed on profits: up to ₹1,00,000 for consumer co-operative societies and up to ₹50,000 for all other types of societies.

section_header:
1970. 
D.—Deductions in respect of other incomes
summary:
**Section 153: Deduction for Interest on Deposits**

*   **Eligible Taxpayers:** This deduction is available to individuals (both general and senior citizens) and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs). However, partners in a firm or members of an Association of Persons/Body of Individuals are explicitly excluded from claiming this deduction on income from deposits held by their entity (Sub-section 3).
*   **Qualified Income Sources:** The deduction applies only to interest income earned from savings accounts or time deposits held with:
    *   Banks covered under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (Sub-1(i));
    *   Co-operative banking societies (Sub-1(ii)); or
    *   Post Offices as defined in the Post Office Act, 2023 (Sub-1(iii)).
*   **Deduction Limits:**
    *   For **non-senior individuals** and **HUFs**: Up to ₹10,000 in interest from *savings accounts only* (excluding time deposits) (Sub-2(a)).
    *   For **senior citizens**: Up to ₹50,000 in interest from *both savings and time deposits* (Sub-2(b)).
*   **Definition of Time Deposits:** The section clarifies that "time deposits" refer to deposits repayable only after a fixed period expires (Sub-4).

**Section 154: Deduction for Disability**

*   **Deduction Amount:** Resident individuals certified as persons with a disability are allowed a deduction of ₹75,000. Those certified with severe disability are allowed a higher deduction of ₹1,25,000 (Sub-1).
*   **Mandatory Conditions:** To claim this benefit, the taxpayer must:
    *   Furnish a copy of the medical certificate issued by the relevant medical authority (Sub-2(a));
    *   Submit the certificate in the prescribed form and manner along with the income tax return (Sub-2(c)); and
    *   If the certificate specifies a reassessment period, the deduction is suspended until a new certificate is obtained and submitted after the original one expires (Sub-2(b)).
*   **Legal Definitions:** Terms such as "disability," "medical authority," and "person with severe disability" carry the same meanings as defined in the applicable disability legislation referenced in the text (Sub-3).

section_header:
127. 
CHAPTER IX
summary:
*   **Purpose of Chapter IX (Sections 155–127 Header Context):** This chapter establishes the framework for **Rebates and Reliefs** under the bill, specifically addressing income tax reductions for individuals, relief against salary timing distortions, treatment of foreign retirement accounts, and mechanisms to prevent double taxation.
*   **Income Tax Rebates for Low-Income Individuals (Section 156):** A resident individual is entitled to a 100% rebate of income tax (capped at ₹12,500) if their total income does not exceed ₹5 lakh. For income charged under specific provisions (Section 202(1)), a higher rebate applies: 100% of tax payable or ₹60,000 (whichever is less) if income is ≤ ₹12 lakh; otherwise, the tax is calculated on the portion of income up to ₹12 lakh.
*   **Relief for Arrears or Advance Salary (Section 157):** To prevent individuals from being taxed at a disproportionately high rate due to lump-sum receipts (such as arrears, advances, or "profits in lieu of salary"), the Assessing Officer may grant prescribed relief upon application. However, no such relief is granted on income for which specific deductions under Section 19(1) have already been claimed.
*   **Taxation of Foreign Retirement Accounts (Section 158):** Income accrued in specific foreign retirement accounts is not taxed annually in India but is taxed only upon withdrawal or redemption, as prescribed, provided the account holder was a non-resident in India and resident in the host country when opening the account.
*   **Double Taxation Agreements (Section 159):** The Central Government may enter into agreements with other countries or adopt agreements between specified associations to prevent double taxation, promote trade, exchange information to prevent tax evasion, and facilitate tax recovery.
*   **Anti-Avoidance Provisions (Section 159(3)(b)):** These agreements explicitly aim to avoid creating opportunities for tax evasion or avoidance, specifically targeting "treaty-shopping" arrangements intended to indirectly benefit residents of third countries in an unjustified manner.
*   **Cap on Deductions (Section 155(2)):** A general limitation exists stating that any deductions allowed under this chapter cannot exceed the total income tax computed on the assessee's total income before such deductions are applied.

section_header: Chapter XI shall apply to the assessee, even if such provisions are not beneficial to
summary:
*   **Mandatory Application of Chapter XI:** The provisions of Chapter XI apply to the assessee regardless of whether those provisions are beneficial to them, ensuring uniform compliance.
*   **Definition Hierarchy for Terms (Section 159(7)):** A specific order of precedence is established for interpreting terms in International Tax Agreements: first, definitions within the agreement itself; second, definitions in the Income Tax Act; third, definitions in Central Government notifications; and finally, definitions in other Central Government tax laws or general laws.
*   **Eligibility Criteria for Non-Residents (Section 159(8)):** Non-resident individuals claiming relief under an International Tax Agreement must obtain a certificate of residency from the authorities of the other country and provide other prescribed documents and information.
*   **Double Taxation Relief (Unilateral) (Section 160(1)):** An Indian resident who pays income tax on foreign-sourced income in a country with *no* Bilateral Tax Agreement is entitled to a deduction from their Indian tax liability.
*   **Computation of Deduction (Section 160(1)-(2)):** The deduction for double taxation is calculated on the doubly taxed income at the **lower** of the Indian tax rate or the tax rate of the other country. If the rates are equal, the Indian tax rate applies. This rule also extends to non-residents claiming their share of income from a resident registered firm.
*   **Statutory Definitions for Calculation (Section 160(3)):** "Indian rate of tax" is defined as the Indian income-tax (after general relief but before this specific double taxation relief) divided by total income. "Rate of tax of the said country" is defined as the tax and super-tax actually paid abroad (after local reliefs) divided by the total income assessed in that country.

section_header:
CHAPTER X 
SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO AVOIDANCE OF TAX
summary:
*   **Purpose & Scope:** Chapter X (Sections 161–162) eliminates the ability to manipulate tax liability through "transfer pricing" by mandating that transactions between associated enterprises must be priced as if the parties were independent (Arm’s Length Principle).
*   **Valuation Rule (Section 161(1-3)):** Income, expenses, and interest arising from international or specified domestic transactions must be determined based on arm’s length prices (ALP). This includes costs apportioned or contributed by associated enterprises for shared benefits, services, or facilities.
*   **Anti-Avoidance Safety Valve (Section 161(4)):** The provisions of Section 161 **do not apply** if adjusting the price to arm’s length would artificially reduce the chargeable income or increase the loss when compared to the figures recorded in the books of account for that tax year.
*   **Definition of Associated Enterprises (Section 162(1-2)):** Two entities are legally deemed "associated" if one participates in the other’s management, control, or capital, or if they share common participants.
*   **Presumptions of Association (Section 162(2)):** Enterprise relationships are presumed associated if specific thresholds are met, including:
    *   One holding **26% or more** of the voting power in the other.
    *   One enterprise’s loans constituting **51% or more** of the other’s total asset book value.
    *   One enterprise guaranteeing **10% or more** of the other’s borrowings.
    *   One enterprise appointing **more than half** of the other’s board or executive directors.
*   **Operational Dependency (Section 162(2)(g-i)):** Entities are associated if one is wholly dependent on the other for intangible assets (patents, know-how) or if there is a significant influence over the supply of raw materials (90%) or sale of goods.
*   **Domestic Transaction Inclusion (Section 162(3)):** For specified domestic transactions, "associated enterprises" also expressly include other units or undertakings of the same assessee involved in transactions under Section 122 or Section 140(9).

section_header: Chapter VIII to which the

or section 144, to which provisions of section 140(9) or (13) are applicable;
summary:
*   **Definition of Specified Domestic Transactions (Section 164):** This section defines "specified domestic transactions" as non-international business dealings (such as those under sections 122, 140(9), 140(13), or 205(4)) entered into by an assessee where the aggregate value exceeds **₹20 crore** in a tax year, subjecting them to Transfer Pricing rules.
*   **Mandatory Pricing Methods (Section 165(1)–(2)):** The arm’s length price (ALP) must be determined using the "most appropriate method" among six listed options (e.g., Cost Plus, Resale Price), selected based on the nature of the transaction, functions performed, and guidelines prescribed by the Board of Income Tax.
*   **Price Determination Logic (Section 165(3)):** If the calculated arm’s length price differs from the actual transaction price by less than the notified threshold (not exceeding 3%), the actual price is accepted. If multiple prices are derived, the ALP is determined as prescribed in the rules.
*   **Assessing Officer’s Powers (Section 165(4)):** The Assessing Officer (AO) may independently determine the ALP if they find that the taxpayer failed to maintain required records (section 168(1)), used unreliable data, failed to respond to section 171(2) notices, or did not charge prices in accordance with the prescribed methods.
*   **Due Process Requirement (Section 165(5)):** Before exercising the power to determine the ALP under section 165(4), the AO is obligated to issue a show-cause notice giving the assessee an opportunity to rebut the proposal based on the AO’s material.
*   **Tax Computation and Deduction Restrictions (Section 165(6)–(7)):** Once the AO determines the ALP, the total income of the assessee must be computed based on this price. Additionally, specific deductions under section 144 (Business Income) or other related sections are disallowed if the transaction is found to be non-arm’s length.

section_header: Chapter VIII in | Chapter XIX-B, the income of the other associated enterprise shall not be recomputed
summary:
*   **Prevention of Double Adjustment (Chapter XIX-B Provision):** If an associated enterprise's income is adjusted under sub-section (6) based on an arm’s length price where tax was deducted at source, the income of the *other* associated enterprise involved in the transaction cannot be recomputed solely due to this specific price determination.
*   **Referral Mechanism (Section 166(1)):** If an Assessing Officer deems it necessary or expedient, they may refer the determination of the arm’s length price for an international or specified domestic transaction to the Transfer Pricing Officer, subject to prior approval by the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner.
*   **Filing of Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) Options (Section 166(2) & (3)):** A reference to the Transfer Pricing Officer cannot be made if a valid option under sub-section (9) (regarding multi-year pricing) has already been declared valid by the Officer; any reference made after such a declaration is treated as if it were never made.
*   **Procedure for Determination (Section 166(4) & (6)):** Upon referral, the Transfer Pricing Officer must notify the assessee to produce evidence. After hearing the assessee’s evidence, considering additional required information, and reviewing all relevant materials, the Officer issues a written order determining the arm’s length price, which is sent to both the Assessing Officer and the assessee.
*   **Multi-Year Pricing Option (Section 166(9)):** The determined arm’s price can be applied to similar transactions for the **two consecutive tax years** immediately following the current year, provided the assessee exercises this option in the prescribed manner and the Transfer Pricing Officer validates it by written order within one month.
*   **Statutory Time Limits (Section 166(7) & (8)):** Transfer Pricing Officer orders must generally be passed at least 60 days before the expiry of the normal assessment limitation period. If fewer than 60 days remain due to specific circumstances under Section 286, the time limit is extended to ensure a minimum 60-day window for the determination.

section_header: Chapter XVI-B.
summary:
*   **Mandatory Alignment with Transfer Pricing Orders:** Under Section 165(11), the Assessing Officer is legally required to compute total income strictly according to the arm’s length price determined by the Transfer Pricing Officer. Section 165(12) extends this obligation to two consecutive tax years if a "valid option" was declared under sub-section (9).
*   **Rectification and Administrative Powers:** The Transfer Pricing Officer may amend orders to correct mistakes apparent from the record (Section 165(13)), and they are empowered to exercise general assessment powers (such as those under sections 246, 252, and 253) to determine arm’s length prices (Section 165(14)).
*   **Guideline Issuance Limits:** The Board may issue guidelines to resolve difficulties in implementing specific sub-sections, subject to Central Government approval (Section 165(15)). However, no new guidelines can be issued after April 1, 2026 (Section 165(16)), and any issued guidelines must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for review (Section 165(17)).
*   **Definition of Transfer Pricing Officer:** Section 165(18) defines the "Transfer Pricing Officer" as a Joint, Deputy, or Assistant Commissioner specifically authorized by the Board to perform certain Assessing Officer functions regarding international transactions.
*   **Safe Harbour Rules:** Section 167 establishes that income determination and arm's length prices are subject to "safe harbour" rules. Under these rules, income-tax authorities must accept the transfer price or income declared by the assessee if specific safe harbour conditions are met (Section 167(3)).
*   **Advance Pricing Agreements (APA) Authority:** Section 168 allows the Board, with Central Government approval, to enter into APAs that pre-determine arm’s length prices or income methods for international transactions (Section 168(1)). These agreements are binding on both the taxpayer and tax authorities (Section 168(5)) and are valid for up to five consecutive tax years (Section 168(4)).
*   **APA Exceptions and Voidance:** An APA is not binding if there is a material change in law or facts (Section 168(6)). Furthermore, the Board can declare an APA void *ab initio* if it was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation, in which case standard tax laws apply as if the agreement never existed (Sections 168(7)–168(8)).

section_header: 172. Every person who has entered into an international transaction or
summary:
*   **Mandatory Accountant Report (Sec. 172):** Any person entering into an international transaction or a specified domestic transaction is obligated to obtain a report from an accountant and submit it in the prescribed form, signed and verified, by the "specified date" (defined in Sec. 173 as one month before the normal income tax return due date).
*   **Key Definitions for Transfer Pricing (Sec. 173):** The section defines critical terms including:
    *   **Arm’s Length Price:** The price agreed upon between independent parties (associated enterprises) in uncontrolled conditions.
    *   **Enterprise & Permanent Establishment:** Broad definitions covering any person or fixed place of business engaged in production, services, investment, or intellectual property rights.
    *   **Transaction:** Includes any arrangement, understanding, or concerted action, regardless of whether it is formal, written, or legally enforceable.
*   **Anti-Avoidance for Non-Resident Income (Sec. 174(1) & (2):** If a domestic person ("first mentioned person") acquires rights to income that would otherwise be payable to a non-resident due to a transfer of assets, that income is deemed to be the domestic person's taxable income, even if it would not normally be chargeable under other provisions.
*   **Capital Sum Coordination (Sec. 174(3)):** If the domestic person receives a capital sum connected to the asset transfer, any income that became the non-resident's income due to that transfer is also deemed to be the domestic person's income.
*   **Prevention of Double Taxation (Sec. 174(4)):** If income is already taxed under this section, subsequent receipt of that same income (in any form) by the same person will not be taxed twice.
*   **Exception for Bona Fide Transactions (Sec. 174(5)):** The provisions of Sec. 174 do not apply if the taxpayer satisfies the Assessing Officer that the transfer and associated operations were *bona fide* commercial transactions and were not designed, directly or indirectly, to avoid tax liability.
*   **Interpretive Clauses (Sec. 174(6)):** References to assets include shares or obligations related to those assets, and any foreign-incorporated body corporate is treated as a non-resident for the purposes of this section.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B, the tax shall be deducted at the
summary:
*   **Limitation on Interest Deduction (Section 177(1), 177(4)):** This section restricts the deductibility of interest paid by an Indian company or permanent establishment of a foreign company in India on debts issued by associated enterprises (AEs) that are non-residents. The "excess interest" subject to restriction is defined as the lower of: (i) total interest exceeding 30% of the borrower's EBITDA, or (ii) the total interest paid to AEs in that tax year.
*   **Threshold Exemption (Section 177(1)(b)):** The restriction only applies if the total interest expenditure on such debt exceeds Indian Rupees 1 Crore in a tax year; amounts below this threshold are fully deductible.
*   **Deeming Provision for Guarantees (Section 177(2)):** A debt issued by a non-associated enterprise lender is deemed to be issued by an associated enterprise if an AE provides an implicit or explicit guarantee for the debt or deposits matching funds with the lender, thereby bringing it under the interest limitation regime.
*   **Carry-Forward of Denied Deduction (Section 177(5), 177(6)):** Interest expenditure that is not allowed as a deduction in the current year due to the excess limit can be carried forward for up to eight subsequent tax years. It may be deducted in future years only to the extent that the "maximum allowable interest" (per the limit in sub-section 4) is not exceeded.
*   **Key Exceptions (Section 177(3)):** The interest limitation rules do not apply to:
    *   Interest paid to a permanent establishment in India of a non-resident bank.
    *   Indian companies or permanent establishments engaged in banking, insurance, or acting as Finance Companies located in an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC).
*   **TDS Rate for Notified Jurisdictions (Unnumbered Clause at Top):** For persons located in notified jurisdictional areas (defined in clause 6 of the preceding context), tax must be deducted at source at the highest of: (a) the rate in force, (b) the rate specified in the Act, or (c) a flat rate of 30%.
*   **Definitions (Section 177(7)):** The section defines "debt" broadly to include loans, financial instruments, finance leases, and derivatives that generate deductible finance charges. "Finance Company" is specifically defined with reference to the International Financial Services Centres Authority (Finance Company) Regulations, 2021.

section_header:
CHAPTER XI 
GENERAL ANTI-AVOIDANCE RULE
summary:
*   **Purpose (Sections 178–179):** This chapter establishes India's General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), empowering tax authorities to disregard or recharacterize arrangements whose main purpose is to obtain tax benefits, regardless of other provisions in the Income Tax Act.
*   **Definition of IAAs (Section 179):** An "Impermissible Avoidance Arrangement" (IAA) is defined as any transaction where the primary intent is tax benefit and which either lacks commercial substance, involves non-arm's length dealings, misuses legal provisions, or is not conducted in a bona fide manner.
*   **Presumption of Intent (Section 179(2):** If any step within an arrangement has a main purpose of tax benefit, the entire arrangement is presumed to be an IAA unless the taxpayer proves otherwise.
*   **Deeming Rules for Commercial Substance (Section 180):** An arrangement is deemed to lack commercial substance if it involves round-trip financing, accommodating parties, offsetting elements, disguised funds, or if tax benefits are the only significant effect on business risks or cash flows.
*   **Specific Identifiers (Section 180(2)-(3)):** "Round trip financing" is broadly defined to include any series of transactions moving funds without substantial commercial purpose, regardless of timing, traceability, or mode. Factors like the duration of the arrangement or the payment of taxes during it are not sufficient to prove commercial substance.
*   **Tax Consequences (Section 181):** If an IAA is declared, the tax authority can determine tax consequences in any appropriate manner, including denying treaty benefits, disregarding specific steps, combining entities, or looking through corporate structures.
*   **Recharacterization Powers (Section 181(2)):** Authorities may treat equity as debt (or vice versa), merge connected persons or accommodating parties into a single entity, and reallocate income, deductions, or the situs of assets to prevent tax avoidance.

section_header: 182. In this Chapter, in determining whether a tax benefit exists,— | 183. The provisions of this Chapter–– | 184. In this Chapter, unless the context otherwise requires,—
summary:
*   **Purpose of Section 182 (Anti-Avoidance Mechanisms):** This section establishes rules for determining if a "tax benefit" exists, authorizing tax authorities to look through arrangements involving connected parties. It permits treating connected persons as a single entity, disregarding "accommodating parties," and ignoring corporate structures that are used solely to obtain tax advantages.
*   **Application of Chapters (Section 183):** The provisions of this chapter apply either in addition to or in lieu of other methods for determining tax liability. Their application is subject to guidelines and conditions prescribed by the government.
*   **Definition of "Accommodating Party" (Section 184(1)):** An accommodating party is anyone whose primary purpose in participating in an arrangement, directly or indirectly, is to secure a tax benefit for the taxpayer, regardless of whether they are related to the taxpayer.
**Key Obligations/Rights and Definitions (Section 184):**
    *   **"Arrangement" (184(2)):** Broadly defined to include any step in a transaction, scheme, or understanding, including unenforceable agreements and property alienations.
    *   **"Tax Benefit" (184(11)):** Covers any reduction, avoidance, or deferral of tax (including under treaties), increase in refunds, reduction in total income, or increase in losses.
*   **Definition of "Connected Person" (Section 184(5)):** Extensively defines connections through relatives, directors, partners, or members of companies, firms, and HUFs. It includes entities with a "substantial interest" in each other's businesses.
*   **Threshold for "Substantial Interest" (Section 184(9)):** A person is deemed to have a substantial interest if they beneficially own at least **20% of the voting power** (for companies) or are entitled to at least **20% of the profits** (for other businesses) at any time during the financial year.
*   **Other Definitions (Section 184):**
    *   **"Relative" (184(8)):** As defined in Section 92(5)(g).
    *   **"Asset" (184(3)):** Includes property or rights of any kind.
    *   **"Party" (184(7)):** Includes a person or permanent establishment participating in an arrangement.
    *   **"Tax Treaty" (184(12)):** Refers to agreements under Section 159(1) or (2).
*   **Penalties/Exceptions:** No specific penalties are listed in these sections; however, Sections 182-183 imply that engaging in such arrangements may result in tax liability being determined differently (i.e., the tax benefit being negated) based on the broad definitions provided.

section_header:
CHAPTER XII 
MODE OF PAYMENT IN CERTAIN CASES ETC.
summary:
**Purpose:** Chapter XII restricts cash transactions for specific financial dealings to promote a traceable and "cashless" economy by mandating digital or banked payment modes for high-value transactions.

**Key Obligations & Thresholds:**
*   **Taking/Accepting Large Amounts (Sec. 185):** No person can accept loans, deposits, or "specified sums" if the total (including previous unpaid balances) is **₹20,000 or more** unless paid via account payee cheque, bank draft, or electronic clearing system.
*   **Receiving Cash/Loans (Sec. 186):** No person can receive **₹2,00,000 or more** in a single day, single transaction, or related transaction from another person via cash; such receipts must go through prescribed electronic or banked modes.
*   **Repaying Loans (Sec. 188):** Banks, companies, and firms must repay loans or deposits of **₹20,000 or more** (including interest) via account payee instruments or electronic systems, though banks may also credit the borrower's account directly.
*   **Mandatory Digital Payments (Sec. 187):** Businesses with total sales/turnover/gross receipts exceeding **₹50 crore** in the previous tax year must provide facilities to accept payments via prescribed electronic modes.

**Exceptions & Exemptions:**
*   **Exempt Entities:** Transactions involving the Government, banking companies, post office savings banks, co-operative banks, statutory corporations, and Government companies are exempt from the restrictions in Sec. 185 and Sec. 188.
*   **Agricultural Relaxations:** Sec. 185 does not apply if both parties derive only agricultural income and have no other taxable income. The threshold for members of primary agricultural credit societies is raised to **₹2,00,000**.
*   **Government Notification:** The Central Government may notify other institutions, associations, or classes of persons that are exempt from these provisions.

summary:
*   **Section 189 (Definitions):** Establishes key definitions for Chapter XIII, clarifying terms such as "banking company" (per the Banking Regulation Act, 1949), "primary agricultural credit society," and distinguishing between "specified sum" (any money receivable in relation to immovable property transfer) and "specified advance" (money in the nature of an advance for such transfer).
*   **Section 190 (Concessional Tax Deduction):** Grants taxpayers the right to deduct from their final tax liability an amount equal to the tax that would have been payable at the average rate on any portion of their total income that is exempt or non-taxable under the Act.
*   **Section 191 (Provident Fund Balances):** Mandates that if an employee’s accumulated balance from a recognized provident fund is included in total income because exemption under Schedule XI, paragraph 8 does not apply, the Assessing Officer must calculate the tax strictly according to the provisions in paragraph 9 of Schedule XI.
*   **Section 192 (Block Assessment in Search Cases):** Prescribes a flat tax rate of **60%** on the total income determined during a "block period" in search and seizure cases, with any applicable central government surcharge added to this amount.
*   **Section 193 (Tax on Global Depository Receipts - GDRs):** Provides preferential tax rates for resident employees of Indian knowledge-based companies (IT/ITES) receiving income from GDRs:
    *   **10%** tax on dividends from GDRs acquired under specified ESOS (Employee Stock Option Schemes).
    *   **12.5%** tax on long-term capital gains from the transfer of such GDRs.
*   **Section 193 (Calculation & Exclusions):** Specifies that for GDR income under Section 193(1), the gross total income is reduced by these amounts before allowing other deductions, and the indexation benefit under Section 72(6) is excluded for calculating long-term capital gains on these GDRs.
*   **Key Definitions in Section 193:** Defines "Global Depository Receipts" (created by Overseas Depository Banks against Indian listed shares or foreign currency convertible bonds), "Information Technology Software/Service," and "Overseas Depository Bank" to scope the applicability of the preferential tax rates.

summary:
*   **Purpose:** This section establishes specific fixed rates of tax (Final Tax) for particular types of income, distinguishing them from the general income tax rates by providing for reduced or flat taxation with strict limitations on deductions.
*   **Gambling and Betting (Clause 1 & 5):** Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, horse races, card games, and other gambling are taxed at a flat **30%** with no expenses allowed as deductions; net winnings from online games are also taxed at **30%** (as computed).
*   **Patent Royalties (Clause 2):** Royalty income from patents developed and registered in India is taxed at a reduced rate of **10%** if the assesseee opts for this scheme. "Developed" is defined as incurring at least 75% of the invention's expenditure in India.
*   **Virtual Digital Assets (Clause 4):** Income from the transfer of virtual digital assets (such as cryptocurrencies) is taxed at a flat **30%**, allowing only the cost of acquisition as a deduction; no other expenses, losses, or carry-forwards are permitted.
*   **Carbon Credits (Clause 3):** Income derived from the transfer of carbon credits is taxed at a flat **10%**, with no deductions for expenditure or allowance allowed.
*   **Life Insurance Business (Clause 6):** Profits and gains from life insurance business attract a special tax rate of **12.5%** with no deductions allowed.
*   **Compliance and Penalties (Clause 2, Sub-clause c):** If an eligible patent holder claims the 10% royalty tax benefit but fails to include this income in their return for any of the next five tax years, they become ineligible for the 10% rate for five subsequent years.

section_header:
105. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Tax on short- | Chapter VII of the Finance (No. 2)
summary:
*   **Section 105 (Context):** This section categorizes specific intangible asset activities—such as transferring patent rights, licensing patents, imparting technical knowledge related to patents, or rendering related services—as distinct income categories for tax assessment purposes.
*   **Section 195 (Penalty/Nondeductible Income):** If an assessee’s total income includes amounts under Sections 102–106 (likely offshore or specific foreign income), this amount is taxed at a special flat rate of **60%**.
*   **Section 195(2) (Restriction on Deductions):** No deductions, allowances, or loss set-offs are permitted against the income taxed under Section 195(1), ensuring the 60% rate is applied to the gross amount.
*   **Section 196(1) (STCG on Listed Assets):** Short-term capital gains (STCG) arising from the transfer of equity shares, units of equity-oriented funds, or units of business trusts that are subject to Securities Transaction Tax (STT) are taxed at a preferential rate of **20%**.
*   **Section 196(2) (Individual/HUF Exemption Threshold):** For resident individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), if the total income (excluding the STCG) is below the basic exemption limit, the STCG is reduced by the amount of that shortfall before the 20% tax is applied, effectively allowing a portion of the gains to be tax-free.
*   **Section 196(3) (IFSC Exception):** The preferential tax provisions of Section 196(1)(b) do not apply to transactions undertaken on recognized stock exchanges located in International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) where the consideration is paid in foreign currency.

section_header: Chapter VIII shall be | Chapter VIII shall be allowed as if the gross
summary:
*   **Purpose and Valuation Method (Section 197, Sub-sections 1, 3 & 4):** This section establishes the method for calculating tax on long-term capital gains (LTCG), generally taxing these gains separately at a flat rate of 12.5% added to the tax on the remaining income. However, for residents transferring land or buildings acquired before July 23, 2024, sub-section (3) allows taxpayers to ignore any excess tax if calculating the gain using the "indexed cost of acquisition" (inflation-adjusted) and a 20% tax rate yields a lower tax liability under the specific formula provided.
*   **Resident Taxpayer Relief (Section 197, Sub-section 2):** Residents who are individuals or Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) receive a tax benefit if their total income (excluding LTCG) is below the basic exemption limit. In such cases, the LTCG is reduced by the amount by which the income falls short of the tax-free threshold, with tax applied only to the remaining balance.
*   **Holding Period and Indexing (Section 197, Subsection 4):** Full deduction under Chapter VIII is permitted for transfers of long-term capital assets if required holding periods are met: 24 months for listed movables, 36 months for unlisted movables/immovables, and 2 years for Securities. Furthermore, sub-section (4) mandates that for unmovable assets not held for 36 months, the cost of acquisition must be the "indexed cost" (adjusted for inflation) to determine if the asset qualifies as "long-term."
*   **198: Special Tax Rate for Equity (Section 198, Sub-section 1):** Regardless of standard rules in Section 197, Section 198 overrides the tax calculation for LTCG arising from the transfer of equity shares, units of equity-oriented funds, or business trusts **if** Securities Transaction Tax (STT) has been paid. These gains are taxed at the standard individual rates applicable to saving bank deposits (CAGR of 6-8% depending on the date), rather than the flat 20% mentioned in the introductory text of Section 197.
*   **198: Exceptions for Equity (Section 198, Sub-section 2):** The preferential tax rate for equity gains in Section 198(1) does **not** apply if: (a) STT was not paid on the transaction; (b) the asset was acquired before April 1, 2015; or (c) the short-term capital gains on unindexed assets exceed 1% of the net sales value.
*   **198: Excluded Entities (Section 198, Sub-sections 3-4):** Section 198 specifically excludes the Government, any local authority, and Companies from the benefits of this special tax provision. Additionally, if "securities" include units of an equity-oriented fund or business trust, the 36-month holding period rule for unindexed assets applies as if the fund were a listed security for the purpose of determining long-term status.
