*   **Tax Rate Structure (Sub-section 2)**: The tax payable is calculated as the aggregate of two amounts: (a) 12.5% tax on long-term capital gains exceeding ₹1,25,000, plus (b) tax on the remainder of the total income (after excluding these specific capital gains) at standard rates.
*   **Low-Income Exemption (Sub-section 3)**: For individuals or Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who are residents, if their total income (excluding long-term capital gains) is below the non-taxable threshold, the capital gains are reduced by the amount by which their income falls short of this threshold before applying the 12.5% tax rate to the balance.
*   **Exceptions & Government Power**: Sub-section (4) exempts transactions undertaken on recognized stock exchanges in International Financial Services Centers (IFSCs) involving foreign currency consideration from specific conditions. Sub-section (5) allows the Central Government to notify specific types of acquisitions where certain provisions do not apply.
*   **Adjustment of Deductions & Rebates (Sub-sections 6 & 7)**: When long-term capital gains form part of gross total income, specific deductions (Chapter VIII) must be allowed from the reduced gross total income, and the rebate under Section 156 must be calculated based on the income-tax payable on the reduced total income.
*   **Definition of Equity Oriented Fund (Sub-section 8)**: An "equity oriented fund" is defined as a mutual fund or unit-linked insurance scheme where: (a) at least 65% of proceeds are invested in listed domestic equity shares; or (b) at least 90% is invested in another listed fund that itself has a minimum 90% equity holding. These percentages are computed using annual averages of monthly opening and closing figures.
*   **New Tax Regime for Manufacturing Companies (Section 199)**: A separate provision allows domestic manufacturing or production companies (registered on or after March 1, 2016) to opt for a flat income-tax rate of 25%, provided they do not claim certain specified deductions and are engaged solely in manufacturing, production, or associated research/distribution activities.

summary:
*   **Purpose of Sections 199 (implied), 200, and 201**: These sections introduce optional, lower tax rate regimes for domestic companies in India, designed to provide tax certainty in exchange for significant changes in accounting and compliance requirements.
*   **22% Optional Tax Rate (Section 200)**: Domestic companies may opt to pay income tax at a flat rate of 22% instead of the standard rates. To qualify, total income must be calculated **without** specific deductions such as capital gains indexation (Chapter VIII-C, excluding Sec. 146) and major incentives listed in Section 205(1).
*   **Loss and Depreciation Barriers (Sections 199(2) & 200(b)-(c))**: When exercising these options, any loss or depreciation attributable to the excluded deductions cannot be set off against current income. Crucially, such losses/depreciation are **deemed fully utilized** (Section 199(2), 200(3)), meaning they cannot be carried forward to reduce tax in future years.
*   **Option Exercise Mechanics (Sections 200(5) & 201)**: The option must be exercised in the prescribed manner before the due date for filing the first return of income under Section 263(1). Once exercised, it applies to subsequent years and generally **cannot be withdrawn** (Section 200(6)).
*   **Permanence and Consequences of Error (Section 200(2) & 200(6))**: If a company fails to meet the requirements of Section 200 in any tax year, the option becomes **invalid** for that year and all subsequent years, and standard tax provisions apply as if the option had never been chosen. Unlike some other provisions, the option under Section 200 cannot be withdrawn unless the person simultaneously exercises the option under Section 200 (referencing the structure of the bill).
*   **23.4% Optional Tax Rate (Section 201)**: A second option allows domestic companies to pay tax at rates specified in a table (Column C), provided they meet specific conditions (Column D, not fully visible in text but implied). This option is subject to Parts A, B, and excluding Sections 199 and 200.
*   **Special Provisions for IFSC (Section 200(4))**: For companies with a Unit in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) that have opted under Section 200(5), specific deductions under Section 116(1) may still be available, provided conditions are met, modifying the standard restrictions on deductions.

*   **Mandatory Income Recomputation:** If an assessee opts out of or becomes ineligible for the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) regime for a tax year (Section 205(1)), the option becomes invalid for that year and all subsequent years. Their total income must be recalculated **without** claiming deductions under Chapter VIII (except Section 146) or specific sections listed in 205(1)(a)–(g) (e.g., Sections 33(8), 45(3), 46, 47(1)(a), 48, 49, and 144).
*   **One-Time Loss and Depreciation Utilization:** Under Section 205(3)(b), any loss carried forward or depreciation attributable to the disallowed deductions must be fully utilized in the current year. Once applied, no further deduction for such specific losses or depreciation is permitted in any later years (Section 205(4)).
*   **Strict Eligibility Criteria for Tax Incentives:** To qualify for the special tax rates under Sections 201 or 204, the business must not be a mere reconstruction or splitting of an existing business (unless revived under Section 140(4)). Additionally, the use of previously used machinery/plant is capped at 20% of the total value, and domestic companies cannot use buildings previously used as hotels or convention centers that claimed specific deductions under the 1961 Act (Section 205(2)).
*   **Restricted Business Scope:** The beneficial tax regime is limited to businesses engaged in the manufacture or production of goods, related research, and their distribution. The business of generating electricity is explicitly included, but the development of computer software in any form or media is excluded (Section 205(6)).
*   **Anti-Avoidance and Transfer Pricing Rules:** The Assessing Officer can override reported profits if transactions with related parties are structured to yield more than ordinary profits. In such cases, profits are determined based on "arm’s length price" principles for specified domestic transactions, and the excess amount is taxed at the higher rates specified in Sections 201(1) or 204(1) (Section 205(5)).
*   **Guideline Sunset and Parliamentary Oversight:** The Board may issue guidelines to clarify conditions regarding new machinery/plant to resolve doubts, but no new guidelines can be issued after April 1, 2026. Any issued guidelines are subject to parliamentary review and modification or annulment, without affecting actions already taken under them (Sections 205(3)–(4)).

*   **Purpose of Section 206:** Establishes the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) regime, requiring specific taxpayers to pay tax on a minimum percentage of their book profit or adjusted total income if the regular income tax payable is lower, thereby preventing excessive tax avoidance.
**Key Obligations and Computation:**
*   **Deemed Income:** If the regular tax payable is less than the threshold, the company’s **book profit** or other entities' **adjusted total income** is deemed to be the total income for that tax year (Section 206(1)(a)).
*   **Applicable Rates:**
    *   **15% of Book Profit:** For most companies (Table Sl. No. 1).
    *   **9% of Book Profit/Adjusted Total Income:** For companies or persons in International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) deriving income solely in convertible foreign exchange (Table Sl. No. 2 & 4).
    *   **18.5% of Adjusted Total Income:** For individuals, firms, LLPs, and other entities not specified elsewhere (Table Sl. No. 3).
    *   **15% of Adjusted Total Income:** For co-operative societies (Table Sl. No. 5).
*   **Book Profit Calculation:** Computed using the formula **B = P + (I - R)** (Section 206(2)), where "P" is the profit in the Statement of Profit and Loss, "I" includes add-backs (like income tax paid, reserves, dividends, and depreciation), and "R" includes deductions (like income exempt under Section 11, depreciation, and deferred tax credits).
*   **Adjusted Total Income:** For non-company entities, this is the total income computed under the Act, increased by specific deductions (such as those under Chapter VIII-C, Section 144, and Section 46) to align more closely with financial accounting standards, subject to the provisions in Note 1.

*   **Tax Credit Mechanism (Sec 10(13)):** Taxpayers who pay Minimum Alternate Tax are entitled to a credit for the difference between the tax paid under this section and the tax payable on total income under normal provisions, which can be utilized in subsequent years.

summary:
*   **Purpose and Scope**: This section (part of Chapter XIX-B) establishes special tax computation rules for **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)**—defined as Indian citizens or persons of Indian origin who are non-residents in India—specifically regarding investment income and long-term capital gains arising from foreign exchange assets.
*   **Key Definitions (Section 212)**: It defines critical terms, including:
    *   **Foreign Exchange Asset**: Specified assets acquired using convertible foreign exchange.
    *   **Specified Asset**: Includes shares in Indian companies, debentures/deposits with public Indian companies, Central Government securities, and other assets notified by the Central Government.
    *   **Investment Income**: Any income derived from a foreign exchange asset.
*   **Restriction on Deductions (Sections 212 & 213)**: An NRI is **not allowed** any deductions for expenditure or allowances under any provision of the Income-tax Act when computing **investment income** (Refer Section 213(1)).
*   **Special Computation for Income Mixes (Section 213(2))**: If an NRI’s total income includes *only* investment income or long-term capital gains (or both), **no deductions** under Chapter VIII are allowed. If other income is also present, the investment/capital gains are reduced from gross total income, and Chapter VIII deductions are applied *only* to the remaining balance.
*   **Tax Calculation (Section 214)**: The income tax payable on an NRI’s total income that includes the specific incomes listed in the table (Column B) is the **aggregate** of the amounts specified in Column C. (Note: The specific values in Columns B and C are not fully provided in the text snippet but indicate a specific tax rate application).
*   **Obligation/Right**: NRIs have a right to tax calculation based on these specific simplified rules, distinguishing their investment/capital gains income from other sources for deduction purposes.
*   **Exceptions/No Penalties**: These sections primarily create computational exceptions for NRIs rather than imposing penalties. They largely restrict the *benefit* of standard deductions to protect the tax base on foreign investment income.

summary:
*   **Capital Gains Exemption for NRIs (Section 215):** Non-resident Indians (NRIs) can defer long-term capital gains tax if they reinvest the net proceeds from selling foreign exchange assets into specific designated assets ("new assets") within six months. The exemption is full if the new asset's cost equals or exceeds the sale proceeds, or partial (calculated by a specific formula) if the cost is lower.
*   **Clawback Mechanism (Section 215(3)):** If the newly acquired asset is sold or converted to cash within three years of acquisition, the previously deferred capital gain becomes immediately taxable in the year of such disposal.
*   **Return Filing Exemption (Section 216):** NRIs are not required to file an income tax return if their total income consists solely of investment income or long-term capital gains, and the applicable tax has already been deducted at source (TDS) under Chapter XIX-B.
*   **Continuity of Benefits for Returning Residents (Section 217):** If an NRI becomes a resident in India, they can continue to benefit from the special tax exemptions for income from foreign exchange assets (excluding shares in Indian companies) by filing a written declaration with the Assessing Officer. This benefit lasts until the underlying assets are transferred or converted to cash.
*   **Opt-Out Option (Section 218):** NRIs may choose to disapply Sections 212–217 for a specific tax year by making a declaration in their return of income. If they opt out, their income is taxed under the general provisions of the Act rather than the specific provisions for NRIs.
*   **Tax Exemption for Bank Branch Conversions (Section 219):** Capital gains arising from the conversion of a foreign bank’s Indian branch into a subsidiary Indian company (as mandated by the Reserve Bank of India) are not chargeable to tax in the year of conversion, provided conditions notified by the Central Government are met.
*   **Reversal of Benefits for Non-Compliance (Section 219(2)-(3)):** If a company fails to comply with the conditions of the conversion scheme or notification, all general provisions of the Act apply without special benefits. Any benefit wrongly claimed shall be deemed to have been incorrectly obtained, potentially subject to recovery.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B shall not apply to the income paid by a
summary:
*   **Tax Exemption for Venture Capital Entities (Chapter XIX-B Exclusion):** The specific tax rules covering venture capital companies and funds (found in Chapter XIX-B) do **not** apply to income paid by these entities to investors, creating a distinct tax treatment for venture capital distributions.
*   **Deemed Receipt for Venture Capital Income (Section 222(5) & (6)):** If venture capital income is not actually paid to a unit holder during a tax year, it is legally "deemed" to have been credited to the unit holder's account on the last day of that tax year in their pro-rata share. Once this income is included in a unit holder's total income, it is **excluded** from taxation in the year it is actually paid, preventing double taxation.
*   **Exception for Specific Investment Funds (Section 222(7)):** The provisions of this section regarding venture capital deemed income do **not** apply to income from investments in funds specified under Section 224(10)(a).
*   **Pass-Through Tax for Business Trusts (Section 223):**
    *   **Nature of Income:** Income distributed by a business trust to unit holders is deemed to retain the same nature (e.g., capital gains, business income) and proportion in the unit holder's hands as it had for the trust (Section 223(1)).
    *   **Trust Tax Liability:** The business trust’s own total income is taxed at the maximum marginal rate (Section 223(2)).
    *   **Capital Gains Exception:** Distributed income classified under specific capital gains heads (Schedule V, Sl. No. 3 or 4) is treated as the unit holder’s income for that tax year (Section 223(3)).
    *   **Reporting Obligation:** The party responsible for distributing income must provide a statement detailing the nature of the income to both the unit holder and the prescribed authority within a prescribed time and form (Section 223(5)).
*   **Transparent Taxation for Investment Funds (Section 224(1)):** Income received or accrued by a unit holder from an investment fund is taxed in the unit holder’s hands **exactly as if** the unit holder had made the underlying investments directly. The fund acts as a tax-transparent vehicle.
*   **Loss Carry-Forward Rules for Investment Funds (Section 224(2)):** If an investment fund incurs a net loss in a tax year that cannot be fully set off against other income, the loss arising from "Profits and gains of business or profession" is allowed to be carried forward and set off by the fund according to specific provisions (text cuts off).

summary:
**Section 115-AD Summarized (Chapter VII)**

• **Purpose**: Establishes tax transparency rules for "Investment Funds" (Category I/II AIFs and IFSC-regulated funds) by treating the fund as fiscally transparent, meaning income and losses are directly attributed to unit holders rather than taxed at the fund level.
• **Loss Treatment (Sub-sections 3 & 4)**: Accumulated investment losses (excluding business/professional losses) existing as of March 31, 2019, are deemed to belong to the unit holders holding units on that date. These losses can be carried forward and set off by the unit holders, and such losses are permanently removed from the investment fund’s books after April 1, 2019.
• **Ignored Losses (Clause b)**: Capital losses arising from units not held for at least 12 consecutive months are ignored for the purposes of calculating the fund's aggregate loss for pass-through.
• **Nature of Income (Section 5)**: Income paid or credited by the fund retains its original nature (e.g., capital gains, interest) in the hands of the beneficiary, effectively treating it as if the beneficiary received it directly.
• **Tax Rate & Unpaid Income (Section 6 & 7)**: The fund’s total income is taxed at rates applicable to companies/firms if the fund is a company/firm, or at the maximum marginal rate otherwise. Income not yet paid out to beneficiaries by year-end is deemed distributed/credited on the last day of the tax year for tax calculation purposes.
• **Prevention of Double Taxation (Section 8)**: Income reported on an accrual basis in one tax year cannot be taxed again in the subsequent year when it is actually paid out to the beneficiary.
• **Compliance Obligations (Section 9)**: The fund manager (person responsible for crediting payments) must submit statements to both the beneficiaries and the Income-Tax Authority within prescribed timelines, detailing the nature and amount of income distributed during the year.
• **Definitions (Section 10)**: Defines "investment fund" specifically as AIFs (Category I/II) regulated by SEBI or funds regulated under IFSCA, including trusts, companies, LLPs, and bodies corporate.

summary:
*   **Purpose and Optional Election**: Sections 225–227 establish the **Tonnage Tax Scheme** for companies operating qualifying ships. Under **Section 225**, a company may *optionally* choose to have its shipping income computed under this special scheme rather than under the standard provisions (Sections 26–54 of the Income-Tax Act).
*   **Definition of "Operating" a Ship**: **Section 226(1)** defines when a company is considered an operator. It includes ships owned or chartered in (including via slot, space, or joint charters). However, a ship chartered out on a **bareboat charter** or **bareboat charter-cum-demise** for **more than three years** does *not* count as a qualifying ship operated by the company.
*   **Separate Business Treatment**: The tonnage tax business is treated as a **separate and distinct business** from all other activities of the company (**Section 226(3)**). Consequently, profits from this business are **computed separately** from profits of any other business (**Section 226(4)**).
*   **Mode of Computation**: If the company opts into the scheme (as per Section 231), it must use the tonnage tax method (**Section 226(2)**). If it does not opt in or is not covered, its shipping profits are taxed under normal income-tax rules (**Section 226(6)**).
*   **Penalties/Tax Exceptions**: Under **Section 226(7)**, once the tonnage income is computed per Section 227 and taxed, the **relevant shipping income** (as defined in Section 228(1)) is **not separately chargeable to tax**. This prevents double taxation.
*   **Calculation Formula**: **Section 227** specifies that the total tonnage income for a tax year is the **aggregate** of the tonnage income for each qualifying ship, calculated as:  
    **TI = DTI × N**  
    Where:  
    *   **TI** = Tonnage Income of the ship  
    *   **DTI** = Daily Tonnage Income (determined by the ship’s net tonnage, per a specified table)  
    *   **N** = Number of days the ship was operated as a qualifying ship during the tax year.

summary:
*   **Tonnage Tax Slabs (Clauses 2-4):** Specifies a progressive tax rate structure based on vessel tonnage: ₹700 base plus ₹53 per 100 tons exceeding 1,000 tons; ₹5,470 base plus ₹42 per 100 tons exceeding 10,000 tons; and ₹11,770 base plus ₹29 per 100 tons exceeding 25,000 tons.
*   **Definition and Calculation of Tonnage (Section 4(4)):** "Tonnage" is defined as the figure cited in valid certificates, inclusive of "deemed tonnage" for slot charters and break-bulk arrangements, to ensure consistent valuation across different contractual structures.
*   **Rounding Rules (Section 4(5)):** Vessel tonnage must be rounded to the nearest multiple of 100 tons for calculation purposes; amounts of 50 tons or more are rounded up, while amounts less than 50 tons are rounded down.
*   **Tax Computation Constraints (Section 4(6)):** No deductions or set-offs are permitted when calculating tonnage income under this Part, overriding any conflicting provisions elsewhere in the Act.
*   **Joint Ownership Provisions (Sections 4(7)-(8)):** When a qualifying ship is operated by multiple companies via joint interest or use agreements, each company’s tonnage income is calculated proportionately to their share or as if they were the sole operator, depending on whether these shares are definitively ascertainable.
*   **Eligible Tonnage Certificates (Section 4(9)):** Valid tonnage must be evidenced by specific certificates, including Merchant Shipping Act rules for Indian-registered ships, Flag State certificates for foreign-registered ships, and the Inland Vessels Act, 2021 for inland vessels.
*   **Scope of Relevant Shipping Income (Section 5(1)-(3)):** Defines "relevant shipping income" as profits from core activities (operating qualifying ships, pooling, affreightment contracts, and specific container/passenger trades) and incidental activities.
*   **Income Limitations and Exclusions (Section 5(2)):** Profits from incidental activities exceeding 0.25% of core activity turnover are excluded from tonnage tax treatment and remain taxable under standard provisions of the Act.

summary:
*   **Losses and Depreciation Handling (Sec. 230):** Pre-existing losses attributable to the tonnage tax business (Section 230(2)) can only be set off against future relevant shipping income, not against other income types (Section 230(3)). Additionally, asset written-down value for depreciation is calculated as if the company had always claimed depreciation during the tonnage tax period (Section 230(1)(d)).
*   **Application for Tonnage Tax (Sec. 231):** Qualifying companies must apply to the Joint Commissioner within three months of incorporation or becoming a "qualifying company" (Section 231(2)). International Financial Services Centre units previously claiming Section 147 deductions have a similar three-month window from when that deduction ceases (Section 231(3)).
*   **Approval Procedure and Rights (Sec. 231(4)-5):** The Joint Commissioner may request documents to verify eligibility and must issue a written order of approval or refusal. Crucially, the company must be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard before any refusal order is passed (Section 231(5)).
*   **Timeline for Orders (Sec. 231(6)):** Approval or refusal orders must be issued within three months of the end of the quarter in which the application was received.
*   **Validity and Termination of Option (Sec. 231(7)-9):** Once approved, the tonnage tax option is valid for ten years from the date of exercise. It ceases to apply if the company loses "qualifying company" status, defaults on specific obligations (Sections 232(1)-(20)), is excluded under Section 234, or voluntarily opts out via written declaration.
*   **Ineligibility Period for New Opt-ins (Sec. 231(12)):** Companies that voluntarily opt out, default on compliance, or are excluded under Section 234(4) are barred from re-joining the tonnage tax scheme for ten years from the date of opt-out, default, or exclusion order.
*   **Mandatory Reserve Contribution (Sec. 232(1)-(2)):** Tonnage tax companies are required to credit at least 20% of their "book profit" (as defined in Section 206(2)) from specified shipping activities into a Tonnage Tax Reserve Account annually.

section_header: 235. In this Part,—
summary:
*   **Purpose:** Section 235 serves as the **definitions clause** for the Tonnage Tax Part of the bill, establishing the specific legal meanings of key terms to regulate the taxation of shipping companies.
*   **Eligible Entities (Section 235(h)):** A **"qualifying company"** is defined as an Indian company with its effective management in India, whose main business is operating ships and which owns at least one **"qualifying ship."**
    *   *Note:* "Place of effective management" is determined by where the board of directors or executive directors make strategic decisions.
*   **Eligible Vessels (Section 235(i)):** A **"qualifying ship"** must be a seagoing or inland vessel of **15 net tonnage or more**, duly registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, or the Inland Vessels Act, 2021, with a valid tonnage certificate.
*   **Exclusions from "Qualifying Ship" (Section 235(i)(A)-(G)):** The term does **not** include vessels used primarily for land-based services, **fishing vessels**, **factory ships**, **pleasure crafts**, harbour/river ferries, offshore installations, or any ship used as a fishing vessel for more than **30 days** in a tax year.
*   **Charter Definitions (Section 235(a)-(b)):** It distinguishes between a **"bareboat charter"** (charterer controls the ship and appoints crew) and a **"bareboat charter-cum-demise"** (charter includes the intent to transfer ownership to the charterer after a set period).
*   **Vessel Categories (Section 235(d)-(f), (j)):** Specific definitions are provided for **"factory ships"** (processing fishing produce), **"fishing vessels,"** **"inland vessels,"** **"pleasure crafts"** (sport/recreation), and **"seagoing ships"** (certified by competent authorities).
*   **Tax-Specific Terms (Section 235(k)-(o)):** It defines operational terms for the tax regime, including **"tonnage income,"** **"tonnage tax business,"** **"tonnage tax company,"** and the **"tonnage tax scheme,"** linking them to specific operational activities and profit computation methods within the Act.

section_header: 236. For the purposes of this Act, there shall be the following classes of | 238. The Board may, by notification, direct that any income-tax authority or
summary:
*   **Section 236** defines the hierarchical structure of income-tax authorities in India, ranging from the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) at the top to operational roles like Inspectors and Tax Recovery Officers at the bottom, establishing the principal actors for tax administration.
*   **Section 237** grants the Central Government the power to appoint income-tax authorities and authorize senior officials (such as the Board or Principal Directors) to delegate the appointment of junior staff (below Deputy/Assistant Commissioner level) and necessary executive or ministerial support personnel.
*   **Section 238** empowers the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to issue notifications explicitly defining the subordinate relationships between various income-tax authorities, ensuring a clear chain of command.
*   **Section 239(1)** allows the CBDT to issue binding orders, instructions, and directions to subordinate authorities to ensure the proper administration of the Act, which those authorities and all staff must follow.
*   **Section 239(2)** imposes a critical check on executive power by prohibiting the CBDT from issuing specific directives to force a particular assessment outcome for an individual case or to interfere with the discretionary appellate functions of Joint Commissioners or Commissioners (Appeals), thereby preserving judicial independence in those roles.
*   **Section 239(3)(a)** authorizes the CBDT to issue general or special procedural guidelines for assessment, collection, and penalties, which can be relaxed in specific areas (as listed in the section) for efficiency; these guidelines must be non-prejudicial to taxpayers and may be published for general information.
*   **Section 239(3)(b) & (c)** provides a mechanism to mitigate genuine hardship by allowing the CBDT to authorize authorities to accept late applications/claims (post-deadline) for exemptions, refunds, or reliefs, or to relax procedural requirements, provided the authority is not an appellate officer and the reasons for such relaxation are specified.

section_header: Chapter IV or VIII, where the assessee has failed to comply with | 240. The Board shall adopt and declare a Charter for Taxpayers and issue such (Part 1)
summary:
*   **Taxpayer Rights (Section 240):** The CBDT is mandated to adopt a "Charter for Taxpayers" and issue necessary guidelines to ensure its effective administration, establishing formal rights and expectations for taxpayers.
*   **Pre-Condition for Deductions:** If an assessee fails to meet requirements for claiming a deduction under Chapter IV-VIII, relief is granted only if the failure was due to circumstances beyond their control **and** the requirement is complied with before the assessment is completed.
*   **Delegation of Powers (Section 241(1)-(3)):** The CBDT can issue directions to income-tax authorities to exercise specific powers or perform functions. Higher-ranking authorities may direct lower-ranking ones, and authorities can delegate the power to issue written orders to their subordinates.
*   **Basis for Delegation (Section 241(4)-(5)):** Delegation orders may be based on territorial area, specific persons/classes, types of income, or case categories. The CBDT may specifically authorize senior officials (e.g., Director General, Joint Commissioner) to perform the functions usually assigned to Assessing Officers.
*   **Concurrent Jurisdiction (Section 241(7)):** The CBDT may direct multiple Assessing Officers to concurrently handle cases within the same area or class. In such instances, the lower-ranking officer must follow the directions of the higher-ranking officer, and legal references to "the Assessing Officer" apply to the higher-ranking authority.
*   **Notifications for Compliance (Section 241(8)-(9)):** The CBDT can issue general or special notifications directing specific persons or classes of persons on how to file returns or perform acts under the Act, specifying exactly which authority they must report to.
*   **Jurisdictional Limits (Section 242):** An Assessing Officer’s jurisdiction is strictly limited to the area specified in their directing order. They have jurisdiction over businesses located (or principally located) within that area and over residents of that area.

section_header: 240. The Board shall adopt and declare a Charter for Taxpayers and issue such (Part 2)
summary:
*   **Purpose**: This section outlines the powers of an authorized tax officer to conduct searches, execute seizures, examine witnesses, and attach property during income tax proceedings, specifically extending to digital assets and electronic records.
*   **Seizure and Deemed Seizure Powers (Sub-sections 1 & 4)**: Officers may physically seize books, documents, computer systems, and assets (excluding stock-in-trade). If physical seizure is impracticable due to size or danger, they may issue a "deemed seizure" order prohibiting the owner or possessor from dealing with the item without permission; such orders remain in force for a maximum of 60 days.
*   **Jurisdictional Exceptions (Sub-section 2)**: A Principal Chief Commissioner or equivalent authority may exercise search and seizure powers in their jurisdiction even if they do not have jurisdiction over the specific individual involved, provided that waiting for proper authorization would prejudice revenue interests.
*   **Expanded Search Location (Sub-section 3)**: If an officer reasonably suspects that relevant assets or documents are located in a building, vessel, vehicle, or aircraft not originally listed in the search authorization, they can authorize the search of those additional locations despite other procedural constraints.
*   **Requisition of Assistance (Sub-section 5)**: Authorizing officers can legally require the assistance of police officers, Central Government officers, or approved private entities/persons to aid in search and seizure operations, and such assistance is a mandatory duty.
*   **Examination and Evidence (Sub-section 6)**: Officers may examine on oath any person present who has control or access to the assets, documents, or computer systems being searched; statements made during this examination are admissible as evidence in tax proceedings and can cover all matters relevant to the investigation.
*   **Legal Presumptions (Sub-section 7)**: Assets, documents, or digital spaces found in a person's possession are legally presumed to belong to that person. Additionally, the contents of such records are presumed true, handwriting/signatures are presumed authentic, and electronic communications are presumed exchanged between the parties they purport to involve.
*   **Provisions for Interim Relief (Sub-section 8)**: While the text is cut off, it indicates the authorized officer may provisionally attach property belonging to the assessee by written order during the course of the search to secure revenue.

section_header: 249. The reason to believe or reason to suspect, as referred to in section 247
summary:
*   **Section 249 (Confidentiality)**: The "reason to believe" or "reason to suspect" recorded by income-tax authorities under Sections 247 or 248 is strictly confidential and must not be disclosed to any person, authority, or the Appellate Tribunal.
*   **Section 250(1) (Scope of Recovery)**: The Assessing Officer may recover tax liabilities (including penalties and interest, but excluding advance tax) directly from seized or requisitioned assets. This covers existing liabilities, liabilities determined on or after assessment completion, defaults under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the Companies Act, or the Black Money Act, and liabilities arising from interim settlement board applications.
*   **Section 250(2) & (3) (Asset Release)**: Assets (or portions thereof) may be released to the person from whom they were seized upon application within 30 days of the seizure month. This requires the Assessing Officer to satisfy themselves about the asset's source, recover existing liabilities, and obtain prior approval from designated senior officials (e.g., Principal Chief Commissioner). Any such release must occur within 120 days of the last search/requisition authorization.
*   **Section 250(4) & (5) (Application of Assets)**: Liquid cash seized can be applied directly to discharge liabilities. Non-cash assets can also be applied to remaining undischarged liabilities and are deemed to be under "distraint" (legal seizure for debt recovery), allowing recovery in the manner prescribed by law.
*   **Section 250(6) & (7) (Multi-mode Recovery & Refund)**: Applying seized assets to liabilities does not prevent the Revenue Department from pursuing other recovery modes under the Act. Any remaining assets or proceeds not required to settle the liabilities must be returned to the concerned person immediately.
*   **Section 250(8) & (9) (Compensation Interest)**: The Central Government must pay simple interest at 0.5% per month to the affected person. This interest compensates for the holding of funds above the liability amount, calculated from the end of the 120-day release period until the completion of the assessment or reassessment.
*   **Section 251(1) & (2) (Jurisdiction & Access to Documents)**: If the seizing officer lacks jurisdiction over the person, assets and documents must be handed over to the correct Assessing Officer. The custodian of seized documents (books, electronic media, etc.) must allow the person to make copies or take extracts upon application, at a specified place and time under supervision.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B of this Act, after sunrise and before sunset, enter––
summary:
*   **Purpose & Scope**: This section (likely Section 253, based on context) grants Income-Tax Authorities the power to conduct daytime inspections (sunrise to sunset) of offices, business places, or charitable activity sites to verify accounts, documents, and digital records.
*   **Inspection Rights & Obligations**: Upon entry (Sub-section 4), authorities can require the person in charge (deductor, collector, etc.) to provide facilities for inspecting books, access to electronic media/computer systems, and any relevant information.
*   **Powers Upon Search**: Authorities may place identification marks on documents, make copies/extracts, record sworn statements (oath), and impound books of account for up to 15 days (extendable with approval) but are explicitly prohibited from removing any assets or stock from the premises (Sub-sections 5 and 7).
*   **Verification of Expenses**: If verifying expenses for functions or ceremonies, authorities can post-evently require relevant persons to furnish information and record sworn statements, which can be used as evidence in legal proceedings (Sub-section 8).
*   **Enforcement of Compliance**: If a person refuses or evades cooperation during an inspection, the authority can invoke the powers under Section 246(1) to enforce compliance (Sub-section 9).
*   **High-Level Approval Requirement**: All actions under this section require prior approval from senior officials, specifically the Principal Director General, Director General, Principal Chief Commissioner, or Chief Commissioner (Sub-section 10).
*   **Definition of Authority**: The term "income-tax authority" covers a wide range of officials from Assessing Officers to Commissioners, and specifically includes Inspectors of Income-tax for certain inspection powers, subject to Board specifications (Sub-section 11).

section_header: 255. The Assessing Officer, assessment unit, verification unit, the Joint | 256. The competent authority shall be competent to make any enquiry under
summary:
*   **Inspection of Company Records (Section 255):** Authorized tax officers, including Assessing Officers, Joint Commissioners, and their designated subordinates, have the legal right to inspect and copy registers of company members, debenture holders, or mortgagees to verify information relevant to tax assessments.
*   **Enquiry Powers (Section 256):** The "competent authority" designated for specific enquiries is granted the same powers as an Assessing Officer to conduct investigations and gather necessary details under the Act.
*   **Judicial Status of Proceedings (Section 257):** Proceedings before income-tax authorities are legally deemed judicial proceedings under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the authorities themselves are considered Civil Courts for the purpose of issuing processes under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
*   **Information Sharing with Government Bodies (Section 258(1)):** The Central Board of Direct Taxes or specified authorities may share tax information with other government bodies (such as those handling tax, duty, cess, or foreign exchange) if deemed necessary for public interest or to assist those bodies in their statutory functions.
*   **Information Disclosure to Private Persons (Section 258(2)):** Senior tax authorities may legally release taxpayer information to private individuals upon a formal application, provided they are satisfied it serves the public interest; such decisions are final and cannot be challenged in court.
*   **Restrictions on Information Release (Section 258(3)):** The Central Government may issue notifications restricting the release of information regarding specific classes of assessees to only those authorities explicitly mentioned in the notification, regardless of other laws.
*   **Information Collection for Verification (Section 259):** Prescribed income-tax authorities are empowered to issue notices requiring any person to provide information useful for inquiries or proceedings, which may then be processed according to official schemes.
*   **Faceless and Efficient Administration (Section 260):** The Central Government may establish schemes to streamline information collection and verification processes by reducing direct taxpayer interaction, optimizing resources, and using team-based approaches; these notifications must be laid before Parliament.

section_header: 261. For the purposes of this Chapter, the expressions—
summary:
*   **Purpose**: Section 261 defines key terms used within the specific Chapter of the Income-tax Act, 1961, ensuring uniform interpretation of procedural and enforcement-related concepts such as searches, seizures, and digital assets.
*   **Authority Hierarchy**: It establishes a tiered structure for **"approving authority"** and **"competent authority"** (clauses (a) and (d)), ranging from senior officials like the Principal Director General down to Joint Directors/Commissioners, depending on the specific administrative level required for approvals.
*   **Officer Designations**: Clause (c) identifies **"authorised officers"**—specifically Joint/Additional Directors, Commissioners, and Income-tax/Tax Recovery Officers—who are empowered to execute search or requisition warrants.
*   **Broad Asset Definition**: Clause (b) widens the definition of **"asset"** to explicitly include bullion, jewellery, and valuable articles held in both physical and virtual forms, covering a broader scope of recoverable property.
*   **Digital & Virtual Inclusions**: The section modernizes legal definitions by including **"computer systems"** (clause (e)), encompassing remote/cloud servers and networks, and **"virtual digital space"** (clause (i)), which covers email servers, social media, online banking/trading accounts, websites, and emerging digital platforms.
*   **Seizure Scope**: Clause (g) defines **"material seized"** to include not just physical documents and books of account, but also digital data storage devices and electronic records (e.g., Excel sheets, Word files, and tax software backups), treating these electronically stored figures as valid books of account.
*   **Procedural Timeline**: Clause (f) specifies how to determine the **"date on which the last of the authorisations for search was executed"**—using the date of the last *panchnama* (search record) for physical searches or the date of actual receipt of documents for requisitions under Section 248.
*   **Scope of Proceedings**: Clause (h) defines **"proceeding"** broadly to include any tax-related proceedings under this Act or the Income-tax Act, 1961, whether pending, completed, or commenced after the date of the search or exercise of powers, ensuring continuity in legal process.

section_header:
CHAPTER XV 
RETURN OF INCOME
summary:
*   **Mandatory Allotment Conditions:** Under Section 262(1), individuals must apply for a Permanent Account Number (PAN) if their income exceeds the taxable limit, their business turnover is likely to exceed ₹5 lakh, they are required to file income tax returns, or they (or key officials of non-individual entities) engage in financial transactions aggregating to ₹2.5 lakh or more in a tax year.
*   **Voluntary Application & Usage:** While Section 262(2) allows anyone to voluntarily apply for a PAN, Section 262(3) mandates that all persons must quote their PAN in all tax returns, correspondence with tax authorities, and payment challans.
*   **Aadhaar Integration:** Sections 262(5) through 262(7) link the PAN with the Aadhaar number; eligible individuals must provide their Aadhaar number when applying for a PAN or filing returns, and there is a provision for Aadhaar to be used in lieu of PAN for those who have not yet been allotted a PAN but possess an Aadhaar number.
*   **Penalty for Aadhaar Non-Compliance:** Under Section 262(6)(b), if a person eligible for Aadhaar fails to intimate (disclose) their Aadhaar number to the prescribed income-tax authority, their allotted PAN will be made inoperative.
*   **Single PAN Restriction:** Section 262(8) explicitly prohibits a person from applying for, obtaining, or possessing more than one Permanent Account Number.
*   **Transaction Obligations:** Section 262(9) requires parties entering into prescribed transactions to quote and authenticate their PAN or Aadhaar number in relevant documents, while recipients of such documents must verify this information.
*   **Reporting & Regulatory Powers:** Section 262(4) obligates individuals to notify the Assessing Officer of changes in address or business details, and Section 262(10) grants the Board the power to make rules regarding the form of applications, categories of required documents, and specific exemptions from these provisions.

summary:
*   **Mandatory Filer Categories (Sub-section 1):** This section defines the specific categories of persons required to file an income tax return, including those with income exceeding the exemption limit, specified entities, educational institutions (under section 45(3)(a)), business trusts, investment funds, and persons claiming carry-forward of business/capital gains losses or refund claims under Chapter XX.
*   **Foreign Asset Disclosure (Clause xi):** Resident individuals (other than Not Ordinary Residents) who hold financial or tangible assets outside India (as beneficial owner/signatory) or are beneficiaries of such foreign assets are explicitly required to file returns, enhancing transparency for cross-border assets.
*   **Statutory Due Dates (Sub-section 1(b) & Table):** The filing deadline depends on the taxpayer type:
    *   **31st October:** For individuals/HUFs/firms (or partners of such firms) required to undergo an audit under the Income Tax Act or any other law.
    *   **30th November:** For assesses required to furnish a report under section 172 (typically firms/associations).
    *   **31st July:** For all other taxpayers.
*   **Digital Filing & Documentation (Sub-section 2):** The Board may prescribe rules for electronic filing, specifying forms, verification methods, and digital transmission resources. It also mandates detailed disclosure of exempted income, specific high-value assets, bank/credit card details, and large expenditures.
*   **Partner and Spouse Liability (Table No. 3 & 4):** Partners of firms subject to audit and their spouses (if assessable jointly under section 10) fall under the strict **31st October** deadline. Taxpayers filing section 172 reports have an extended deadline of **30th November**.
*   **Late and Revised Returns (Sub-sections 4 & 5):**
    *   **Late Returns:** Can be filed up to **nine months** after the end of the relevant tax year or before the assessment process is completed.
    *   **Revised Returns:** May be submitted to correct omissions or errors within the same **nine-month** window to ensure accuracy of the filed income.
*   **Updated Returns (Sub-section 6):** Any person (or their representative) may furnish an "updated return" within **forty-eight months** from the end of the financial year following the relevant tax year. This provision allows for income updates (and potential tax adjustments) long after the standard deadline, particularly relevant for loss carry-forward scenarios.

summary:
*   **Ineligibility for Updated Returns (Section 263(6)):** A person is barred from filing an updated return of income if specific scrutiny actions are already underway or concluded against them. This includes cases where an assessment order is under appeal, a show-cause notice under Section 281 is issued (unless exempted), or if the person falls within a class notified by the Board.
*   **Exclusions Based on Investigative Procedures (Section 263(6)(d)):** An individual cannot file an updated return for a tax year if a search, survey, or requisitioning of assets/books has been initiated or conducted against them under Sections 247, 248, or 253. This ineligibility also applies to prior tax years if such actions relate to the current year, including cases where seized assets or documents from others are linked to the filer.
*   **Defective Returns and Cure Periods (Section 263(7)):** If an Assessing Officer deems an updated return defective, they must notify the assessee, who has **15 days** (plus any granted extension) to rectify the defects.
*   **Consequences of Failure to Cure (Section 263(7)(b-c)):** If the defect is not corrected within the allowed time, the return is treated as **invalid**, and the law applies as if no return was filed. However, if corrected after the deadline but before the assessment is finalized, the Assessing Officer may choose to condone the delay and accept the return as valid.
*   **Applicability to Specific Returns (Section 263(8)):** The provisions for updated returns also apply to returns filed pursuant to orders under Section 239. However, there is an exception for **specfied senior citizens** (as defined in Section 402(39)) for relevant tax years where tax was deducted at source.
*   **Key Definitions (Section 263(9)):** The section defines specific terms including:
    *   **Beneficial Owner:** An individual who provided consideration for an asset for their own or another person's benefit.
    *   **Beneficiary:** An individual deriving benefit from an asset where someone else provided the consideration.
    *   **Specified Entity:** A list of entities including research associations, mutual funds, securitization trusts, universities, hospitals, venture capital funds, and various government boards/authorities.
    *   **Specified Laws:** Refers to four specific acts dealing with smuggling, benami transactions, money laundering, and black money.

summary:
*   **Purpose of Section 263 (Tax Return Preparers):** This section establishes the framework for a scheme allowing **tax return preparers** to submit income tax returns on behalf of taxpayers. It strictly limits who can prepare returns to individuals who are **not** employees of the "specified class of persons" (such as auditors) or those prohibited under section 515(3)(a)(ii), ensuring independence and preventing conflicts of interest.
*   **Purpose of Section 265 (Verification of Returns):** This section prescribes **mandatory verification requirements** for income tax returns filed under section 263. It defines specifically **who must verify** the return to ensure the authenticity of the declaration, with different requirements applied based on the legal structure of the taxpayer.
*   **Verification for Individuals (Section 265, Table Row 1):** Returns for individuals must be verified by **the individual themselves**. If the individual is mentally incapacitated, a guardian or competent representative verifies it; otherwise, verification can be done by a person holding a **valid power of attorney**.
*   **Verification for Hindu Undivided Families (Section 265, Table Row 2):** Returns for HUFs must be verified by the **karta** (manager). If the karta is absent from India or mentally incapacitated, verification is conducted by any **other adult member** of the family.
*   **Verification for Standard Companies (Section 265, Table Row 3):** For a typical resident company, the return must be verified by the **managing director**. In the absence of one, or if unverifiable due to unavoidable reasons, any **director** or other prescribed person must verify it.
*   **Special Corporate Scenarios (Section 265, Table Rows 4-7):**
    *   **Non-resident companies:** Verified by a person holding a valid **power of attorney** from the company.
    *   **Companies being wound up or with assets under a receiver:** Verified by the appointed **liquidator**.
    *   **Companies taken over by the Government:** Verified by the **principal officer** of the company.
    *   **Companies under Insolvency Resolution:** Verified by the **insolvency professional** appointed by the Adjudicating Authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

summary:
*   **Authorized Verifiers (Sections 8–13)**: This section specifies the individuals legally permitted to verify tax returns for various entities: a firm’s managing partner (or any non-minor partner if the managing partner is unavailable, **Sec. 8**); a limited liability partnership’s designated partner (or other authorized person if unavailable, **Sec. 9**); a political party’s chief executive officer, **Sec. 11**; any member or principal officer of an association, **Sec. 12**; and the individual or their competent representative for other persons, **Sec. 13**.
*   **Mandatory Pre-Payment (Section 266(1))**: An assessee must pay any remaining tax liability, along with any applicable interest and fees for delays or defaults, *before* furnishing the return. The return must be accompanied by proof of this full payment.
*   **Tax Credit Adjustments (Section 266(2))**: When calculating the final tax payable, the legislation mandates deducting specific pre-paid amounts, including advance tax, tax deducted at source (TDS), reliefs for foreign tax paid (under Sections 159/160), and any eligible tax credits (under Section 206), to determine the net balance due.
*   **Payment Allocation Priority (Section 266(3))**: If the amount paid towards the liability is less than the total tax, interest, and fees due, the payment must be adjusted in the following specific order: first to the fee, second to the interest, and any remaining balance to the principal tax owed.
*   **Interest Calculation Basis (Section 266(4)–(5))**: Interest under Section 423 (for late filing) is computed on the net tax after deducting all eligible credits (such as TDS and advance tax), whereas interest under Section 424 (for late advance tax payment) is calculated based on the shortfall between the assessed tax and the advance tax paid.
*   **Definition of Assessed Tax (Section 266(6))**: For the purpose of calculating interest under Section 424, "assessed tax" is defined as the tax on the total income declared in the return, reduced by the tax deducted or collected at source.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B, on any income which is subject to such deduction or
summary:
*   **Purpose**: This section establishes the **tax liability and payment mechanics** for "updated returns" under Section 263(6), ensuring that any additional tax, interest, and fees are cleared before the updated return is finalized.
*   **Obligations for Non-Filers (Sub-section 267(1))**: If no initial return was filed, the assessee must pay the calculated tax, along with interest for delayed advance tax/return filing and applicable fees, plus any additional tax calculated under sub-section (5).
*   **Obligations for Updaters (Sub-section 267(3))**: If an earlier return was filed, the assessee must pay the additional tax plus interest for delayed advance tax payments. This liability is reduced by any interest paid with the earlier return and any refunds issued for that earlier return.
*   **Credit Deductions (Sub-sections 267(2) & 267(4))**: When calculating the final tax payable, the law mandates adjusting for specific amounts already accounted for, including:
    *   Tax already paid as advance tax.
    *   Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) or Tax Collected at Source (TCS).
    *   Tax reliefs claimed under Sections 157 (Double Tax Avoidance Agreements), 159(1), 160 (Foreign Tax Credit), and 159(2) (Specified territories).
    *   Tax credits for set-off under Section 206(13) (compulsory powers of ITA officer).
*   **Proof of Payment Requirement**: The updated return must be accompanied by **proof of payment** for the main tax, additional income-tax, interest, and fees (Sub-sections 267(1)(c) & 267(3)(c)).
*   **Deemed Default Status (Sub-section 267(8))**: Failure to pay the full amount of tax, interest, or fee as required creates a "deemed default" status for the assessee, triggering all provisions of the Income Tax Act applicable to defaults.
*   **Cumulative Consequences (Sub-section 267(9))**: The provisions for default under sub-section (8) apply **without prejudice** to any other legal consequences or penalties the assessee may independently incur due to non-compliance.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B, on any income which is subject to such deduction or
summary:
*   **Purpose and Scope**: Section 265B (referenced contextually as part of the revision process) allows taxpayers to voluntarily revise a previously filed return to disclose additional income, tax reliefs for foreign tax payments (under Sections 159, 160, 206(13)), or deductions that were omitted from the initial filing.
*   **Categories of Revisions**: Per clauses (b) through (e), the revision must specifically address:
    *   Income subject to tax withholding or collection in India not previously included.
    *   Foreign tax credits or reliefs under Section 159(1) or 160 not previously claimed.
    *   Relief under Section 159(2) for tax paid in specified external territories.
    *   Tax credits set off under Section 206(13).
*   **Staggered Penalty Structure**: Sub-section (5) imposes an "additional income-tax" penalty on the aggregate of tax and interest payable, increasing with the delay in filing the revised return (measured from the end of the financial year succeeding the relevant tax year):
    *   **25% penalty**: If filed after the standard time limit (Section 263(4)/(5)) but within 12 months.
    *   **50% penalty**: If filed between 12 and 24 months.
    *   **60% penalty**: If filed between 24 and 36 months.
    *   **70% penalty**: If filed between 36 and 48 months.
*   **No Extension Beyond 48 Months**: The text implies that the right to file a revised return for credit/relief purposes under this specific penalty structure expires 48 months after the end of the succeeding financial year.
*   **Definition of Tax Base**: Sub-section (6) clarifies that "tax" for the purpose of calculating the penalty includes any surcharge and cess by whatever name called.
*   **Interest Calculation Rule**: Sub-section (7) overrides the standard provision in Section 424(2) for these specific revisions. Interest is calculated based on the **"assessed tax"** of the new return, which is the total income declared after accounting for:
    *   Credits/reliefs claimed in the earlier return (Section 266(1)).
    *   Tax deducted/collected at source.
    *   This ensures interest is computed on the net tax liability rather than potentially gross amounts, preventing double counting of credited amounts in the interest base.

section_header: Chapter XIX-B, on any income which is subject to such deduction or
summary:
*   **Updated Income and Tax Credits (Sub-sections 1–7 context):** This section establishes rules for computing "updated income" by adding any new income, foreign tax reliefs (under Sections 159/160), or tax credits (under Section 206) that were not included in the original return, adjusted by any refunds issued on the earlier return.
*   **Guidelines by the Board (Sub-sections 8–10):** The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) may issue guidelines with Central Government approval to resolve procedural difficulties in implementing this section. However, no new guidelines can be issued after April 1, 2026. Any issued guidelines are subject to Parliamentary scrutiny (30 days) and can be modified or annulled by both Houses of Parliament, though this does not invalidate prior actions taken under those guidelines.
*   **Interest Computation Rules (Sub-sections 11–12):** Specifies how interest is calculated on the updated income. Interest under Section 423 is based on the total income declared in the specific return type (Section 263(6)), while interest under Section 425 accounts for the returned income. If an updated return is filed under Sub-section (1), the interest paid in the earlier return is treated as nil for calculation purposes.
*   **Assessment Procedure and Notices (Section 268(1)):** The Assessing Officer (AO) can serve notices on individuals who have filed a return or whose filing deadline has expired. These notices may require the person to furnish a valid return of income, produce accounts/documents, or provide verified written information, including a statement of all assets and liabilities.
*   **Limits on Document Requests (Section 268(2)):** The AO requires prior approval from the Joint Commissioner to ask for a statement of assets/liabilities not included in standard accounts. Additionally, the AO cannot request accounts older than three years relative to the relevant tax year, unless necessary for specific complex inquiries.
*   **Authority to Order Audits (Section 268(5)):** If the AO determines that an audit is necessary due to complexities, volume, doubts about correctness, or specialized business nature (with high-level administrative approval), they can direct the assessee to have their accounts audited. This direction must be issued after providing the assessee a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

summary:
*   **Purpose and Scope**: This section outlines the procedural framework for the "Assessment" of tax returns filed under Sections 263(1) and 268(1), detailing how tax liabilities or refunds are calculated, adjusted, and determined by the Assessing Officer.
*   **Calculation and Adjustment**: Under sub-section (1), tax, interest, and fees are computed on total income. The final amount payable or refundable is determined by adjusting this amount against taxes deducted/collected at source, advance taxes, rebates, reliefs, and self-assessed payments.
*   **Mandatory Notification and Response**: Before applying adjustments for incorrect claims, the Authority must inform the assessee (sub-section 2(a)). The adjustments become effective if the assessee fails to respond within 30 days; otherwise, the response is considered (sub-section 2(b)).
*   **Time Limits for Intimation**: The department cannot send an intimation of assessment after 9 months from the end of the relevant financial year (sub-section 4). Additionally, if a loss is adjusted resulting in no tax payable or refund, an intimation must still be sent (sub-section 3).
*   **Definitions and Deemed Actions**: Sub-section (5) defines "incorrect claim apparent from any information in the return" as inconsistencies, missing statutory information, or deductions exceeding specified limits. It also deems the return acknowledgment as the final intimation when no tax is payable/no adjustments are made.
*   **Verification Rights (Scrutiny)**: To prevent understatement of income or excessive loss claims, the Assessing Officer can serve a notice within 3 months of the return filing deadline, requiring the assessee to attend an office or produce evidence (sub-sections 8 and 9).
*   **Final Assessment Order**: Following a hearing of evidence, the Assessing Officer issues a written order assessing total income or loss and determining the final sum payable or refund due (sub-section 10).
*   **Special Restrictions for Exempt Entities**: For entities like research associations (listed in Schedule III), no assessment order under Section 11 exemptions can be made unless the Central Government is notified of any contravention and the entity's exemption has been officially withdrawn (sub-sections 11 and 12).

summary:
*   **Purpose and Initiation**: This section (Chapters XI, sub-sections 2–10) establishes the mandatory procedural safeguards for declaring a transaction an "impermissible avoidance arrangement." It requires the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to initiate the process only if they are of the opinion that Chapter XI provisions are applicable.

*   **Mandatory Notice and Opportunity to Be Heard (Sub-sections 2 & 3)**: Before making a declaration, the authority must issue a notice to the assessee detailing the reasons/opinion and provide a minimum opportunity to be heard, which cannot exceed 60 days. If the assessee fails to submit objections within this timeframe, the authority may issue directions to declare the arrangement as impermissible.

*   **Right to Higher Review (Sub-sections 4 & 6)**: If the assessee objects to the notice and the Principal Commissioner/Commissioner remains unsatisfied with the explanation, the matter must be referred to the **Approving Panel**. The Panel then issues final directions on whether to declare the arrangement impermissible and specifies the tax year(s) to which the declaration applies.

*   **Dismissal of Proceedings (Sub-section 5)**: If the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner hears the assessee and concludes that Chapter XI provisions should *not* be invoked, they must communicate this decision in writing to both the Assessing Officer and the assessee, effectively closing the initiation phase.

*   **Procedural Powers of the Approving Panel (Sub-sections 7–9)**:
    *   The Panel must grant a hearing to both the assessee and the Assessing Officer before issuing any direction that is prejudicial to either party (Sub-section 7).
    *   The Panel has the power to direct further inquiries, examine records, or require the assessee to submit additional documents/evidence before making a decision (Sub-section 8).
    *   Decisions by the Panel are made by a majority vote among its members (Sub-section 9).

*   **Finality and Execution (Sub-section 10)**: Once directions are issued by the Principal Commissioner/Commissioner (under Sub-section 3) or the Approving Panel (under Sub-section 6), the Assessing Officer is obligated to complete the pending proceedings strictly in accordance with those directions and the relevant provisions of Chapter XI.

summary:
*   **Cross-Year Application of Avoidance Directions (S. 11):** If the Approving Panel declares an "impermissible avoidance arrangement" for a tax year different from the one currently under assessment, the Assessing Officer (AO) must apply these findings to that other year without seeking a separate direction.
*   **Senior Approval for Assessments (S. 12):** No assessment or reassessment order involving tax consequences determined under Chapter XI (General Anti-Avoidance Rules) can be finalized by the AO without the prior approval of the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner.
*   **Time Limits for Panel Decisions (S. 13–15):** The Approving Panel must issue directions within six months of receiving a reference. However, this timeline is extended if information is sought under international agreements or if court injunctions stay proceedings, ensuring a minimum remaining period of 60 days for decision-making.
*   **Binding Nature and No Appeals (S. 16–17):** Directions issued by the Approving Panel are legally binding on both the assessee and the tax authorities (Principal Commissioner/Commissioner and subordinates). Crucially, no appeal lies under the Act against these specific directions.
*   **Composition of the Approving Panel (S. 18–19):** The Central Government constitutes a three-member Approving Panel consisting of a High Court Judge (Chairperson), a senior IRS officer (Principal Chief Commissioner level or higher), and an academic expert in direct taxes and international trade.
*   **Panel Tenure and Support (S. 20–23):** The Panel’s term is ordinarily one year (extendable to three). The Income-tax Board is required to provide staff support and grants the Panel the same administrative powers as those given to Advance Ruling Boards under Section 387.
*   **Dispute Resolution Procedure (S. 275):** For "eligible assessee" cases, the AO must first issue a draft order detailing any prejudicial variations. The assessee has 30 days to either accept the changes or file objections with both the AO and the Dispute Resolution Panel; failure to object results in the assessment proceeding based on the draft.

summary:
*   **Choice of Accounting Method (Section 276(1) & (2))**: Taxpayers computing income from "Profits and gains of business or profession" or "Income from other sources" may use either the cash or mercantile system of accounting, provided the method is regularly employed. The Central Government has the authority to notify specific income computation and disclosure standards for particular classes of taxpayers or income types.
*   **Enforcement and Recomputation (Section 276(3))**: The Assessing Officer (AO) may recompute income under Section 271 standards if they are dissatisfied with the completeness or correctness of the taxpayer's accounts, if the taxpayer did not regularly follow their declared accounting method, or if the taxpayer failed to comply with the notified standards.
*   **Inventory and Securities Valuation (Section 277)**: Strict rules govern how inventory is valued for business income:
    *   General goods are valued at the lower of actual cost or net realisable value, including all taxes, duties, and fees incurred to bring the goods to their locus standi.
    *   Unlisted or irregularly quoted securities are valued at actual cost initially recognized, while other securities are valued at the lower of cost or net realisable value.
    *   Securities held by scheduled banks or public financial institutions are valued according to notified standards, considering Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines.
    *   Valuation must be done on a category-wise basis for comparing cost and net realisable value.
*   **Timing of Specific Income Recognition (Section 278)**:
    *   Interest on compensation or enhanced compensation is taxable in the year it is received.
    *   Claims for price escalation contracts or export incentives are taxable in the year they achieve reasonable certainty of realization.
    *   Certain specified incomes (referenced in Section 2(49)(w)) are taxable in the year received if not previously taxed.
*   **Reassessment of Escaped Income (Section 279)**: If income has escaped assessment, the AO may assess/reassess that income or recompute losses, depreciation, and deductions. Crucially, the AO can also assess "other issues" noticed during these proceedings, even if procedural compliance for those specific issues wasn't followed initially.
*   **Procedural Safeguards and Notices (Section 280)**: Before reassessing under Section 279, the AO must issue a notice allowing the taxpayer up to three months to file a return of income for the relevant year. This return is treated similarly to a standard return under Section 263. No such notice can be issued without specific information suggesting income has been escaped from assessment.

Time limit for | 284. The specified authority for the purposes of sections 280 and 281 shall be
summary:
*   **Section 280** establishes the time limits for issuing "show cause" notices regarding escaped income. Generally, no notice can be issued after four years from the end of the relevant tax year.
*   For high-value cases where the escaped income is likely ₹50 lakh or more, the time limit extends, but the notice cannot be issued after six years and three months from the end of the tax year, provided the Assessing Officer has sufficient evidence or documents.
*   **Section 281** restricts notices regarding income that may have escaped tax, prohibiting issuance after four years generally, or after six years (but not exceeding that period) for cases involving income of ₹50 lakh or more.
*   Both Sections 280 and 281 mandate a waiting period: **no notices shall be issued within one year** from the end of the tax year to allow for normal assessment processes to conclude.
*   **Section 283** creates an exception allowing notices to be issued at any time (bypassing standard time limits) if required to implement findings from appellate authorities, tribunals, courts, or directions from the Approving Panel under Section 274(6).
*   This exception in Section 283 does not apply if the original assessment would have been barred by time limits when the appeal was filed or when the reference was made to the Approving Panel.
*   **Section 284** specifies that the "specified authority" who must sanction the issuance of these notices is the Additional Commissioner, Additional Director, Joint Commissioner, or Joint Director.
*   **Section 285** stipulates that tax is charged at the normal rates applicable if the income had not been escaped; it also allows the Assessing Officer to drop proceedings if the taxpayer claims they were already correctly assessed and have not appealed the original order.

summary:
*   **Purpose**: This section establishes the **time limits** for completing assessment, reassessment, and recomputation proceedings under the Income-tax Act, requiring the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to finish these actions within a specified period.
*   **Standard Time Limit**: For the majority of listed scenarios, the deadline for completion is fixed at **one year** from a specific trigger event.
*   **Trigger Events**: The one-year clock starts from the end of the **financial year** in which:
    *   An updated return of income is furnished under Section 263(6) [Clause 2].
    *   A return is furnished consequent to an order under Section 239(3)(b) [Clause 3].
    *   A notice under Section 280 is served [Clause 4].
*   **Order-Based Triggers**: The one-year clock starts from the end of the financial year in which an appellate or consequential order is **received or passed** by the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner in cases of:
    *   Fresh assessment requests under Sections 359, 363, 377, or 378 [Clause 5].
    *   Implementing findings from Sections 359, 363, 365(10), 368, 377, or 378, or Court orders [Clause 8].
*   **Month-Based Triggers**: The one-year clock starts from the end of the **month** in which:
    *   An assessment or reassessment stands revived under Section 153A(2) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 [Clause 6].
    *   An assessment order for a firm is passed, necessitating an assessment on a partner [Clause 7].
*   **Procedural Enforcement**: Clauses 9 and 10 ensure that even when an order merely requires verification of documents or provides an opportunity for a hearing (rather than a fresh assessment), the administrative process to give effect to the appellate order must be completed within one year.

summary:
*   **Purpose & Scope**: This section defines the statutory time limits for completing income tax assessments, reassessments, and recomputations, particularly focusing on cases involving Transfer Pricing (TP) and international transactions governed by the International Taxpayer and Investment Facilitation Act.
*   **Primary Time Limits**:
    *   For standard assessment/reassessment linked to orders under sections 359, 363, 365(10), or 368, or 377/378, the deadline is the **end of the month** in which the relevant order is received/passed, plus **six months** (extendable to **nine months** with approval).
    *   For modification of assessment to give effect to order under section 166 read with section 377, the time limit is **two months** from the end of the month the order is received by the Assessing Officer.
*   **Transfer Pricing Extension**: Under clause (2), if the case involves a reference to the Transfer Pricing Officer for determining the arm’s length price under section 166(1), the time limit specified in sub-section (1) is extended by an additional **twelve months**.
*   **Excluded Periods (Clause 3)**: The clock stops (these periods are excluded from the calculation) during specific delays caused by:
    *   Reopening proceedings at the assessee's request or re-hearing under section 244.
    *   Court-ordered stays on assessment proceedings.
    *   Delays due to issues under Schedule III or section 270(11)(i) (e.g., withdrawal of approvals).
    *   Periods required for mandatory audits, inventory valuations, or responses to valuations under sections 268(5) and 269(1).
    *   Processing of declarations under section 375 (capped at 60 days), Advance Rulings under section 383, information exchange under international agreements (capped at 1 year), and proceedings for impermissible avoidance arrangements under section 274.
    *   Searches/requisitions under sections 247/248 (capped at 180 days) until items are handed over to the correct jurisdiction.
*   **Minimum Remaining Time Guarantee (Clauses 4 & 5)**: If, after excluding the periods mentioned in clause (3), the remaining time for the Assessing Officer to complete the assessment is **less than 60 days**, it is automatically extended to **60 days**. This also applies if the Transfer Pricing Officer’s period is already extended to 60 days under section 166(8).

summary:
*   **Purpose and Authority**: Section 288 empowers the Assessing Officer to modify, recompute, or amend prior income tax assessments to amend total income, ensuring that individual taxpayers' liabilities accurately reflect changes determined in their respective entities (firms, associations, etc.) or following fraud investigations.
*   **General Time Limit**: Except for specific cases, these actions must generally be taken within **four years** from the timing specified in the section's table (typically the end of the financial year in which the triggering order for the firm/body was passed).
*   **Partnership Adjustments (Sl. No. 1)**: The officer may amend a partner’s assessment if remuneration was previously allowed but later found non-deductible under Section 35(f), triggered by the firm’s reassessment or specific revisional orders.
*   **Association/Body Share Adjustments (Sl. No. 2)**: The officer may amend or correct the assessment of a member of an Association of Persons (AOP) or Body of Individuals (BOI) if their share of income was initially omitted from their personal assessment or calculated incorrectly due to changes in the entity’s income.
*   **Fraud and Recomputation (Sl. No. 3)**: If proceedings are initiated under **Section 279** (concealment of income), the officer must recompute the assessee’s total income for subsequent years to adjust for carried-forward losses or depreciation allowances that may no longer be valid.
*   **Procedural Continuity**: The procedural provisions of **Section 287** apply to these amendments as far as possible, ensuring standard due process is followed during these corrections.
